1. You have to go at the "Settings".



2. Check on the left side at "My Settings" for "Edit Signature".



3. Under the "Edit Signature" you can see the "Signature Picture".



There are 2 options
Option 1 - Upload your image from a URL
Option 2 - Upload your image from your computer

You picture has to be 500 Width and 100 Height and a maximum size of 30.000 bytes.

4. After uploding your picture, click "Upload".



And you're done.

*Note: DO NOT use inappropriate content.*

Breakdown Brickforce Map - Progress Topic & Recruitment

Original Map Concept

The original concept I had developed in my brain while awaiting for my Beta Key. Excited that I finally got it, I wanted to implement a bit of work into the map I had thought up! The original concept for Breakdown is this: It will consist of three major layers. The Underground, The Midfloor (Earthlevel), and then the Topfloor (Skylevel).

Not only that, I have also thought up several ideas as to how I will build this, how the tunnels in the underground will look etc. The map will be placed on a 100x100 default map with several layers of Dark Stone Brick surronding the tunnels, and being the leveling floor right before the dirt and grass for the Midfloor.

6 Major buildings will connect to make up the Midfloor, along with some open space to run around them, etc.

I will add more to this section later.

Recruitment

If you would like to participate in the building of Breakdown, you may contact me via forums with a PM saying that you are willing to join and contribute atleast 1+ hour of work to the map. If you contribute atleast one hour of work with me developing the map, I will put your name on the builder list below!

Although this site is brand new, we wish to obtain feedback from the community on different aspects. What would make it better? Hopefully we will start getting a good crowd of players that can help further the development with new ideas and suggestions.

Current Project Plans:
  • Map Critics - These persons will be a part of the Map World Team. Each map when uploaded as a registered map, should be visited by a critic and a respectful review ill follow. See website for how critics review maps.
  • Personal Blogs/Wiki - Although this is not something we have included, we may include this for those whom are dedicating time in maps, updating frequently, releasing new maps, so on and so forth. This is to help them be able to post Update Notes, keep players up-to-date on content, and have their own space to do whatever with.
  • Clan Support - We want to provide a place for clan activities along with personal Clan Forums. Although this is a very tedious job for us admins, it is something we are willing to do. As of now, the way it is planned is to allow each Clan Leader the right to accept group members and kick group members. Clan board will only be viewable by that clan.

Staff we are currently looking for and what their job descriptions will be:
  • Moderator - Moderators will keep tabs on each forum to ensure proper rules are being followed. This also includes being a major part of the process of updating threads with new content and website information.
  • News Team - These are BFMAPWORLD Writers. We need you guys to help with writing articles such as newly released content from Brick Force. Once we get the Blog/Wiki running, we can move you guys there for more space.
  • Graphics Team - Do you like developing Graphics for others? Well that is what your job will be. Signatures, Avatars, and special requests.

If you have any questions and would like more information, please reply to this thread or send me a pm. I will do my best to respond back as soon as possible.

Launzhime war story.
---
Chapter 1.

10 years ago, there was a war, a war so large it made everyone worried. It was in a place known as Launzhime. The world was in fear. They thought the war would come to their home town. For some, they were lucky. Some, no so much. The war branched out over most parts of the world. This war ended a very long time ago. The Northern Forces were led by their leader, King Kalibann. Kalibann had killed over 500 people before the war even started. It was rough, seeing that many people murdered. And to think, they were all Southern Forces. The Southern Forces were led by Queen Resifialda. The Northern Forces invested in the technology called drones. The drones were very powerful machines built for protecting the Northen Forces themselves. The Northern Forces would do anything to try and stop us. They were pure evil. They had no regard for human life. They only considered the lives of their forces.
---
Well... How is it?

**All content in this post belongs to boopboop**

Chapter 2.

It's been 10 years since the last war in Launzhime. We, the Southern Forces have been keeping a close watch on the Northern Forces. They seemed to be building more drones! We, over the years have gained some drones of our own. We call them counter drones. Mainly just to protect the Southern Forces and the people who do not agree with Kalibann's choices. These Counter drones were built to be more powerful than the Northern Force's drones. The Northern Force's drones have very powerful energy beams. Our drones have the same, except we also have a "Havens strike" attack. It's a space drone. It shoots a laser, 3x as powerful as the normal drone's laser to a specific spot on the Earth. These lasers can lead to major crater in the Earth and other plants alike. the crater are much worse than the ones on the moon. Much bigger than some of the biggest crater there. The lazar is powerful, and we have it. The only reason the Northern Forces have not went to war yet is that they're afraid of our "Havens Striker" and they really should be.

**All content in this post belongs to boopboop**

Chapter 3.

The next day we were checking all of our drones to make sure they were all working, but just when we were about to go get some items from one of the ships, we get a message.

To: Southern Forces commanders.
From: Northern Forces commanders.
You are getting a warning. If you do not remove all of your defenses we will attack. You have 1 hour to do so. It is your choice of whether we release Doomdrones.
-King Kalibann.

I must tell Queen Resifialda at once!
|As he made his way to the castle, he saw a Doomdrone along the coast. He started to run. As soon as he got to the Queen, she declared war.|
I don’t know how this will turn out, but I am a trained Scout. My job is to scout out the area and to kill anyone who attacks me. I keep a close watch to everything. I was going to head to the coast. There it was. There was a Doomdrone coming closer to the beach. Following it were 4 Northern Forces Battleships and a Dreadnaught. A Dreadnaught was a mother ship. It’s the main ship. It holds 5 water cannons, is very large with 3 floors. And can house over 300 people in the main decks. I have come to reason two reasons there is a Dreadnaught. One: They are transporting people to go to war. Or two: They are transporting drones to wipe us out. We have set up our Havens Striker. It’s ready to fire as soon as needed. This could be bad.
|They all waited there. Silent. Waiting. Until they heard a large explosion. It came from the market! He went to the market to see what had happened. There was a drone in the market marked Northern Forces. It was a stealth drone. It is very small, but packs a punch. It’s very fast and can go almost anywhere that is a 1 meter x 1 meter area.|
I got a drone and commanded it to go to the market to take care of the stealth drone.

The Spy drone didn’t stand a chance against the normal drone. As I was walking back to the coast I saw this very bright light. It looked to be coming closer to me. It fell right in front of me. It was a thing that looked like a cast for the arm. But it was very high tech. I put it on, still not knowing what it was. I saw that it had an old time trigger. You had to put your fingers in the holes, then pull back. I did that, and a laser came out. It was a laser shooter. This was not any old laser though. It was a blue laser. It is more powerful than the red lasers used by most drones. I shot at a rock. When all the dust cleared, the rock was gone. Left behind was a large hole. It seemed that upon every use of the laser, the laser grew stronger. I rushed back to the coast. The Doom Drone was on the beach now. I fired at it with my laser shooter. It was not very hard to aim right to the Doom Drone’s weak spot. The Doom Drone stopped in its place, and then fell. It was done, destroyed. We still had the Battleships and Dreadnaught. I fired at it. I took down all of the Battleships but the Dreadnaught fired at us. They seemed to have a mounted laser shooter. It shot Purple lasers. Purple lasers are the most powerful lasers known by the Southern Forces, and the Northern Forces have it! This could be bad. They fired right at me. I had to doge 4 shots. It also seemed that with every shot they took the laser would gain more power. We’ll see how this turns out.

The heat of day wore on, the sun scorching hot overhead.
Hero of the rebels, Jack Cyrus, or Jack, as his friends called him.
He was the leader of J-Squad, named in homer of him.
His friends, Mark and John, were with him, they were scouting ahead of the army.
"Why must we do this?"moaned Mark.Jack's steely gray eyes flashed at him.
"WHY are we doing this"?!? roared Jack,"We have REBELED, chosen to be free of the king"!!
"Yes, but why?" asked John, less whiny than Mark."Okay",sighed Jack,"I'll tell you why."
"Three years ago, the people were happy with the king.All was well.Then,we noticed(some of us) that taxes were soaring, food was short,and people were abused.I could stand it until that one day when it snapped.
I had just got home when I heard a scream.It was my mother! I ran to her room just as two men were climbing out the window. I was too late. The damage was done. It was because we didn't give enough grain to the king, so he bumped her off. Father never came home that night. Others hated the king too, so we got help from a neighboring kingdom, and started the war."
"So, always remember what we are fighting for,
Justice."
---------------------------------------
Well, what do you think so far?

Btw, whoever wants to contribute to the story can message me the details, after saying so here.
I'll take three donors to start with.
You've got something with this. I am enjoyed what was here so far, so continue writing. Good job. I will continue to read this for sure!

Thanks!
----------------------------------------
Chapter 2,Capture

Now our hero Jack gets up and says,"Come on guys,let's keep looking."
His friends followed him to a valley. "Now what?",asked John. "Look around in there, the army will have to go through it."said Jack,"Scout for anything amiss."they split up, searching for the traps the nasty king would be sure to have laid.
They searched for hours not finding anything. Then,John spoke up,"Wait a minute, hold it!" The others stopped and stared in in surprise at him."What if the king didn't lay traps here, maybe...." "Speak up!" Said Jack. "Well, what if the only trap here, is for US?" They heard a rumbling sound, turned, and saw boulders! Boulders rolling towards them!! "Run!!!" Yelled Jack, and took off running away.They ran until the boulders piled up, at the entrance where the army had to come through. "We need to clear that entrance! They rebels depend on us!!" Yelled Jack, running back to the pile. "That'll take YEARS to move!"wailed Mark. "There are many secrets not yet discovered." Jack said, with a twinkle in his eyes. He ran to the fallen boulders, scooped up some black dirt with his handkerchief, and ran to the boulders. He stuck the handkerchief in the rocks, found two stones, banged them together over the handkerchief. The handkerchief caught on fire, and Jack ran to them and dragged them into a cave! "What in the" began John, when,BOOM! a loud explosion rocked the valley. After a little while, they went out the passageway was clear, but the rocks blocked the way back to the road. "Let's go this way." Said Jack. They walked until they heard the tromping of feet. They enemy was coming!
They ducked into a cave and.... ..the king's soldiers were there to capture them. They tried to fight, but a knight is hard to punch, especially through armor.
"About that passageway thing..." Began Mark. "Hush!" Said one knight ,"You are to be taken to the king. Gunther!!" Shouted a knight "Rig up the traps in the valley." It was then that they realized, the army was in peril.
If they can't escape, the entire army would be crushed.

Chapter 3, The King

The walk was exausting.
The knights were making them walk to the king's castle, to be presented before him.
"Why must we walk all the way?" whined Mark.
"So you don't run off on a horse, now shush up." said one knight.
They finally saw the castle walls, rising up out of the ground.
The gaurd yelled over the wall "So you caught them!"
"Yes, we caught them easy, the skulking rats." the knight replied.
The massive gate opened up, like the mouth of a giant.
They were led through the gates, up a flight of stairs, and led through a door.
There, on a giant throne, sat the beastly king. He was at the end of a huge room, almost leering at them.
"You caught them." the king spoke to them, for the first time.
Before the knight could respond, the king said, "Put them in their cells."
They were led to the dungeon, locked them up, and left them.
"Another fine mess we got in to." moaned Mark.
They were shut up for several days, with two meals a day.
Finally, they were brought before the king again.
"For being a traitor to us, we hereby sentence you to death in the arena." the king said.
They were filled with dread at this mention.
The way the arena worked was there was a table on one side, they were on another side.
Savage beasts were released in the center of the arena.
If they could kill the beasts, they would be pardoned.
If they did not, then death would follow.
They were let in through the gate to the arena floor.
The crowd roared.
The beasts snarled.
They were lifted in.
There was no way out anymore.

title: Comparison Between The 3 Best Nintendo Animating Programs

posts.h:
Flipnote Studio

Supports sound
Has only a few colors
Has online support (until May 31, 2013)
Has onionskin feature and other features
Has different brushes
No SD export

Inchworm Animation

No sound support in animating
Has unlimited colors
No online support
Has onionskin feature and other features
Has different brushes
SD export support (.SWF, .BMP sequence)

Flipnote Studio 3D

Has sound support
Has more colors than in its predecessor, but less than in Inchworm Animation
Has online support
Has different brushes
SD export support (.AVI, .GIF)

Hope this helps

I breathed heavily as I watched my Grunt opponent lay on the ground before me, completely out cold. The "sudden-death" match was basically how well you could balance on a platform with a rounded bottom, and if anyone fell off, they would instantly be out. The Grunt had lost his patience and tried to ring me out himself, but I managed to avoid him and he went flying off. And thus, my first victory.

I was returned to the training room that I had been sent to before to prepare myself for the next opponent. The ground was almost covered with wrestling mats, and there were several punching bags near a post that could be set up, along with a wooden manikin that was shaped rather oddly, which I assumed was for practicing with blades, which were a rather common natural weapon for Sporeverse creatures. Rather than actually using the various types of equipment, I took this time just to recover from the last battle that I had. Considering that I had barely defeated one of weakest intelligent Sporeverse creatures, my odds didn't seem too good for the next fight.

Interrupting my thoughts, an Omegasect guard burst through the door, signaling for me to follow him with his serrated scythe arm. Apparently half an hour lasted a lot shorter when I was preoccupied with my brain.

I stood on the opposite end of the oval-shaped dirt arena than my opponent. This creature was a particularly strange one, known as the Aerogan. I had never seen one before, but I had researched an awful lot on their race. Even though they are generally a peace-loving empire, they are very rough on their enemies, and have a military force that compliments that. They have green bodies that are striped black in a tiger-like patter, with a long, almost snake-like body with legs that looked too short to carry the body for long. They have dragon-like claws and overall a dragon-like shape, especially the flare of green feathers and fins that decorated the neck, like a collar for the large-toothed head.


Just like last time, the announcer, who stood confidently on top of his tall brick tower, introduced the two fighters and really stressed the details of what he predicted would come during the fight. When he finally ended his pointless speech, he began saying:

"Fighter one, are you ready?" A nod from the Aerogan followed. "Alright. Fighter two, are you ready?" I nodded my head slowly and nervously. "Then... BEGIN!"

This opponent was clearly much more patient than the last. He advanced on me slowly, and I mimicked his movements, until we were circling each other, both waiting for the other to attack, almost on instinct. There was a good fifteen feet between me and my enemy, and so I took the time to try and remember what these guys could do in a fight. Alright... um... They have... claws and wings. Both something I'll have to watch for... I tried to recall my small amount of research. There was another thing... something with their mouths... a breath attack, was it? Yes, that has to be it. Let's see... it can't kill me, I know that... but... what does it do again?

The dark, misty form of the shadowy figure sat on his luxurious throne, surrounded by his many experiments in alchemy. Moonlight shone through the window that was placed behind the massive chair, and purple curtains were closed, blocking out most of the luminous white. Tables were set to the sides of the room, four in all, two to each side. Variously colored mists rose from beakers and flasks, tubes lad from one container to another, and colors shone dully from inside their respective containers, creating a small, dim rainbow of pinks, purples, greens, and blues. A large pair of doors sat in front of the throne, which formed a tall pentagonal shape when closed together. The throne was raised slightly, with a purple and black carpet leading up the few steps in front of the magnificent chair. A vaguely humanoid figure sat upon the strange throne, wispy bits of smoke and etheral gasses leaking from his incorpreal form. Two black skeletal beings knelt before him, only respecting the ghostly being out of complete and utter fear.

"And... what happened to them?" The shade asked with a wispy voice that sounded like the very essence of death.
"Oh, I'm sure Shadow handled Melody and her little gang there." One of the skeletons stammered, daring only to tilt his head up slightly. "You know how he's rarely done you wrong before!"
"He's only never wronged me because I had never assigned a task as dire as this one." The spirit hissed.
"But... but... I'm sure he would stop at nothing to get things done, your highness."
The left door slowly creaked open, and a humanoid head poked through first, then the rest of the body emerged, showing the body of a human, though obviously too dark to point out an details.
"I apologize for my tardiness, my lord." the figure bowed respectfully. "The portal didn't behave as expected."
"Nevermind that..." The ghostly form said "Have you completed your task?"
"Well..." Shadow started uncomfortably "Mostly. Melody and that Anixian character are as dead as possible for me, I assure you. Flametorch is completely unaware that the knife had poison inside, and no one seems to be suspecting anything, so he should be dead within 24 hours. All that's left is Tomlotr, GraveBear, IcyTea, StarCloud, and that nuisance Daxflame."
"Hm. Are you sure that your mission is complete?"
"Yes, Sire."
"Then... why can I see this?" A circular image formed with a purple rim surrounding the outside. The image inside could be seen as if looking through a window. It showed several brick-people, two who were gaining consciousness and being cared for by medics, and two that seemed to be having a discussion.
"But... your highness, there's no way! I was sure that they were dead! I truly was! I... I... how... they couldn't have survived! They-" Shadow's words were cut off by the grasp of powerful magic that formed at his throat in the form of dark particles, choking him and lifting him into the air.
"It is obvious that I overestimated your abilities, Shadow. Not only have you failed to kill Anixian and Melody, even when you caught them entirely by surprise, but you have also failed in finishing off Flametorch as well. Wasn't GraveBear also one of the major threats to our plan? Wasn't he at the battle site as well?"
"Sire... I-"
"SILENCE! We have many foes that are going to be much stronger than the ones that you faced today. If you can't even handle them, then I have no use for you anymore..."
"Sir, please! *Ack!* No! Pl-"
The black matter surrounded Shadow, and with one loud boom, all the particles-and Shadow himself- imploded into nothingness.

"You two!" The two skeletons immediately dropped back to their knees at the sound of their master's voice. "I need one of you to drop down onto the Brick-World, and another on Minecraftia. Find beings on those worlds that would be willing to join forces with us."
"But, your highness, how would we know who to talk to?" One of the skeletal twins stammered. Two purple gems, each about the size of a nickel, formed above the two minions and fell into their grasps.
"When the right one is near, the crystal will glow. Oh, and don't worry, there is always someone in search of respect and power and will be willing to do anything to earn it. We just have to know where to look. Your task is to go to each world and find one of those beings."
"Very well Sire." The two skeletons said in perfect unison.
"Good. Now, off with you two! I have much more important things to do than this." Then, both skeletons simultaneously burst into clouds of dark particles, vanishing each into their assigned worlds. With a wave of his hand, the shade created an image similar to the one he had created before, but this one showing particularly on Melody.
"MelodyC of the Brick-world," the ghostly figure said, "So young, and yet so mysterious. Perhaps killing her would have been a mistake. Yes, all the better to find her and harness the vast power that she has."

I couldn't react fast enough before a half dozen 4-inch long toxic spikes flew from my enemy's tail and into my shoulder, giving me several wounds there. I felt like I would faint from the pain alone. The empty sockets on the tip of the Aerogan's tail instantly regrew their lost spikes. I could barely keep standing, not just because of the pain in my shoulder, but also because the poison from four different spikes were leaking into my bloodstream all at the same time (Two of them missed, I forgot to mention.).

"Hmph. I pity you, creature. Not having any claws or wings, no horns or poison, nothing to fight me with. And yet you somehow manage to keep on fighting." The Aerogan mocked.
"Well... there's one thing I do have." I yanked out two spikes out of my shoulder vigorously. "A brain."
They weren't exactly daggers, but it was the only weapon I could have for the moment. Also, the refs couldn't penalize it, because they were technically natural weapons: They never said they had to be my weapons. The Aerogan seemed unmoved.
"Sorry to break this to you, but I am immune to my own toxins." He then charged straight at me, using his wings to lift him a few inches off the ground. I reacted quickly enough to get out of the way and spin around with my "dagger", stabbing it directly into the center of his back.
"Who said I was relying on toxins?" I countered, readying myself for another assault. My opponent spun back around to face me, and a purplish gas began to form around his maw.
"You know, I do have attacks that you can't turn back against me..." The Aerogan hissed. He lifted his head up and then whipped it back down again. On the descent, his mouth popped open like a machine was operating it, and then several baseball-sized purple spheres flew out and in my direction, each one trailing purple poison mist, like a jet plane in flight, but rounder. Oh, my thoughts came back to me, THAT'S what the breath weapon was. But thinking up those two sentences somehow delayed my reaction enough that the purple orbs crashed into me, sending transparent purple liquids spilling all over my body and soaking my clothes. The impact alone was enough to make me rear back a little.

Then the effects came. A soft burning sensation cloaked most of my body, like leaving a seat-warmer on in a car for too long.
"And...?" I said, trying to act unaffected by the attack.
"Oh, don't worry," my enemy said, "in a few moments you'll certainly feel it." And then I did.
The soft heat slowly intensified. Soon it felt like someone had pressed a match against my clothes. Then it felt like someone had pressed a match against my clothes after soaking me in lighter fluid. I couldn't help but let out a scream before crashing to the ground. One could literally see smoke trailing off my body.
"Game. Set. Match." The Aerogan gladiator mocked, looking down at the humanoid form that was rolling around in pain from the breath weapon. "Keep in mind that you can surrender anytime you want." The insults kept coming. "You do know that it can only get worse from here."

I wanted so desperately to quit. Just so that I wouldn't have to experience another moment of the burns. Everything around me went blurry, my hearing began failing. I knew that all effects like this would all dissipate eventually, leaving me relatively battle-ready again, but the Aerogan gladiator could do almost anything he wanted while I was in my vulnerable state. And I highly doubted that he'd just let me sit there if I wasn't quitting. Boy was I right.

I suddenly felt a heavy impact on my shoulder, which was powerful enough to force me to roll onto my other side. I felt another hit on the back of my head. Come on... I urged myself, If you lose this, there's no way you'll be leaving the planet. Suddenly, I felt myself being lifted off the ground. There were a few moments of ascent, and then I had a zero-gravity feeling briefly before slamming into the dirt again, sending intense pain signals flying up my nerves. Still the relentless assault continued. I was battered, beaten, tossed around, slammed, kicked, slashed, and spiked. MY subconscious kept slipping into my thoughts more commonly. You can just surrender, I kept thinking. It took all my willpower not to scream out about it. Eventually, I was wondering if what I felt was just a result of the beating, and the actual acid effects had already worn out.

Suddenly, the flaming sensations cooled down. Within moments, the only pain I felt was from the harsh attacks that the Aerogan dealt to me.
"Hm. You persist." my enemy said, surprised, as he watched me get back to my feet. "I have to say I'm impressed. I never would have guessed that something as seemingly fragile as yourself could withstand all that."
"It helps to be raised on a planet where military strength and fighting skills are extremely important." I admitted, still struggling to stand. I yanked out the remaining two needles that had been fired at me earlier.
"But you still don't seem to have the strength to continue fighting..." the Aerogan noted.
"Give me all that you've got!" I taunted, "I can take it!"
"Whatever you say..." my opponent leaped into the air, and then expanded his bat-like wings to fly upward, until he seemed to be only about the size of a dime from where I stood. Then the shape hovered for a few slight moments and then grew. I jumped out of the way of the high-speed nosedive, half hoping for him to miss and crash into the ground. But that wish didn't come true. Instead of the catastrophic failure that I had expected, my opponent swung his body back up into the air, only gently brushing the ground. Then he repeated the strategy, dive-bombing me again. But this time I was ready for it.

I stood my ground, waiting for the perfect moment to execute my plan. When my foe finally became close enough, I swung my hands upward, and my body fell back. I caught hold of the strange mane around the Aerogans neck,yanking him back down when he tried to go aloft again. I then wrapped my arm around his mouth, and stomped hard on the tail to hold it in place. My other hand went around the neck. There wouldn't be any tricks this time.
"Mhphffgpmmhmmm." The Aerogan tried to say, glaring at me.
"Looks like I got you." I said, trying my best not to loosen my grip at all.
"Hmmphmmh." Was the reply.
"Looks like it's my turn to make an offer. Give up, and I'll let your head go?"
"Nhhmmmphh Mmhhhhpp!"
I squeezed harder.
"HMM! HMM!" The enemy's head started shaking up and down violently. I let go, and the Aerogan instantly jumped back, gulping in as much air as he could.
"And Daxflame of the Brick-People is victorious!" The announcer called form his tower. Everyone in the crowd (Except the Aerogans) went wild. It still felt weird having my race being referred to as "Brick-People", even when I obviously wasn't bricky in this galaxy.

One more opponent, I thought, and I'm home free.

"And now, for the second of the three final rounds, we have Daxflame of the Brickman Empire versus Shelf of the Barrafin Empire!" The announcer called form his safe tower to the audience, while both fighters stared down each other.
I did know a few things about Barrafins. They were huge enemies of the Merfolk Lords, though the two Empires share many similarities. There were a variety of classes that Barrifin fighters chose from, though I only remembered four: General, Soldier, Illusionist, and Scientist. Based on the robe-like outfit and mystical-looking braces, rings, and belt, I decided that Shelf was most likely and Illusionist. Illusionists often rely on some fancy gear and equipment that have effects that apparently seemed like "magic". They also used such abilities to delay, distract, or trick their enemies. But since that none of the special accessories were allowed use in the competition, I was awfully curious about how Shelf managed to make it this deep into the tournament.


"Fighter one, are you ready?" The announcer yelled at me form his tower. I nodded. "Fighter two, are you ready?"
"You better believe I am!" Shelf called back, sounding a bit too confident.
"Then... GO!"

Like the Aerogan, Mr. Barrafin didn't come straight at me and attack. Rather, he advanced slowly, decreasing the distance between us while I just stood there, wondering what the heck he was doing. Maybe Shelf made it the same way I did, I thought, maybe this is going to be a battle of wits, not physical endurance.
Soon Shelf was barely further than arm's length away. I took my chance to attack, stepping forward and throwing as much force as I could into a single punch. What I found was my hand being bounced of something metal, my wrist being grabbed, and me being tossed over Shelf's shoulder. Dang, my mind instinctively said, this guy's stronger than I thought. I got back up to my feet, surprised that the Barrafin wasn't continuing his assault. The next few moments were just the two fighters circling each other, like I did with the Aerogan, but at much closer range.
"What? Not another attack?" Shelf taunted, "You bore me, Brickman."
"Why don't you hit me?" I countered, "Do I look like I can defend myself that easily?"
"Actually, considering that you made it this far without weapons, I would expect that your mind alone is enough for defense."
"I could say the same about you."
"Sorry, but I do have weapons, you just don't know where they are..."
Next thing I knew, dust found it's way into my eyes from the ground. Then several claws scratched me, followed by the feeling of a massive metal shoe bashing me into the chest, forcing me onto the ground. I then endured several more kicks while I got the dirt out of my eyes. As soon as it was out, I jumped back up to face my enemy. Shelf stood in front of me, his arms folded like he had some type of authority over me.
"Well, that's not exactly what I had expected..." he started. I did a high kick, interrupting him, but his clawed hands grabbed my ankle and brought me mack to the ground, slamming my entire body and face into the dirt. Dust rose up around my collapsed form. "But that I did expect."
I wriggled free of the grasp and jumped right back up. I was trying to think of my own dirty trick to use on my opponent, but nothing immediately came to mind. Another few moments passed with no actions whatsoever, but then Shelf swung his hand at lightning speeds. When I went to block, I had his metal boot slam into my vulnerable torso, knocking the wind right out of my stomach.
"I can't say I'm impressed." Shelf went on, "In fact, I'm a bit disappointed."

Blightblade, the leader of the Reaperspikes and commander of their army, sat in his office alone with a large monitor sitting on a chair on the other side of the room. It was night on their home planet, so there was no light other than the small candle that had been placed on Blightblade's desk, even though the room had electric lighting.Papers cluttered the sides of the wide desk, to make room for the candle. The room was quite small, and had one wooden door and two small windowsills, though they let in no moonlight. The room was decorated with a technological galactic map on one wall, and a painting of a battle site on the other. The monitor sat on top of a cushioned chair, across from its owner, and shown a black and purple ghostly figure sitting on a throne in and equally dark room.

"And this ship, where did it crash?" the figure asked angrily.
"We shot it down above the planet of Stonage, and we figured that it crashed near the capitol city." Blightblade reported. "But you can't expect us to go down there. The Omegasects would annihilate any of the ships that we send withing their borders, let alone near their home planet. Even the ships that we sent to shoot 'Daxflame' down were destroyed moments after he crashed."
"Hmm..." the spirit muttered, "That would prove to be inconvenient, wouldn't it? But you do want this weapon, no?"
"Of course."
"Then you'll have to find its creator, who just happens to be on Stonage. Unless, of course, you'll be willing to send your armada outside of the Sporeverse..."
Blight was stunned. "Outside of the Sporeverse? No one's done that yet and survived! But, if the need arises... where would you have us go?"
"There's a place just barely on the outside of one of the galaxy's spiral arms, known locally as the 'imagispere'. This is the place where I reside."
Blight did some quick calculations before answering to the misty, ghost-like being. "We'd be much more likely to make it to Stonage and back, even if it meant battling back the Omegasects... I'll see what I can do."
"Good..." The ghost said back. "I will ask for a report in due time. Do not let me down, Blightblade."
"I will try my hardest." Blight said back, and the monitor screen went black.

* * *

The ghostly form almost chuckled. Blight had absolutely no idea that he was just speaking with an etheral being that had much bigger plans than conquering a small galaxy. No, it was much, much bigger than that. The weapon was a source of power for anything that wished to use it, whether it was technology or magical. But, linked to the spirit, the weapon could do much more catastrophic damage, which was highly favored. And then, this "MelodyC" often thought about a place where there was a "reactor", which would enhance the capabilities of the weapon even more.
"And, if I were to combine myself with he power, I could also escape this etheral existence and return to my true self. And, best of all, no one suspects anything yet. Yes, soon, there will be a new era; the second rise of the Phantom Lord is about to come."

Shelf's crystal-spiked tail whipped around as he spun, and I just barely dodged the attack. The most annoying thing is that Shelf wore some sort of armor which wouldn't let me simply punch or kick him, which is what I mostly did to the last two combatants.

I swept him off his feet with my leg, and he collapsed to the ground, only to jump back up half a second later.
"Hm... this battle is obviously getting nowhere..." Shelf stated.
"Maybe if you attacked more, then someone could actually win." I countered.
"But it is fairly obvious to me that you only won by catching opponents off guard after they attack you," he replied. "If I were to strike more, I'd likely be subject to the same strategy." We had returned to our circular walk.
"You do have a point." I admitted, trying my hardest not to show any kind of weakness. Suddenly, the tail returned and forced me back into the dust on the ground. I could've sworn that the left side of my skull had just been shattered.
"The key is getting your enemy off guard." Shelf taunted, "Which seems to be especially effective on you."
 With the hand behind my back, I gathered as much dirt and dust as I could in one fist.
"Well, getting up, Brick-man?" Shelf muttered at me.
"Just give me a moment... I want to-" I leaped up and tossed the dust at Shelf's face. It all seemed to go straight for his massive eyes, like metal dust to a magnet. It was a very simple and predictable trick, but it worked.

In the few seconds that the dust trick gave me, I did a low sweep on Shelf with my leg, knocking him to the ground. The next thing I did was stomp on his hard-armored chest, which didn't seem to hurt to much, but it was worth a shot. When Shelf recovered, I immediately kicked his lower jaw. I needed a weapon. Just any sort of weapon. My normal physical assault didn't do very much, so I needed something. Anything.

A golden glint caught my eye. Quickly I dived for it and yanked Shelf's arm brace right off of him. As soon as he had a sense of freedom, Shelf leaped back up into fighting position.
"And what's that supposed to do? You're not allowed to use that sort of thing, you know." He muttered.
"There's no rule against using it as a melee weapon!" I said, secretly hoping that it was true.

By then we both had it. It was obvious that we were both too smart for each other, which is really something I didn't know was possible. Both fighters dived into battle. The fight that followed was some sort of wrestling match combined with MMA and maybe a slight hint of football tackles. Both fighters were relentlessly striking each other, always to close for the other to perform some sort of evade-and-counter tactic. Eventually, I couldn't even remember why we started fighting in the first place. All that I knew (And all the Shelf knew, probably) was that I needed to win. Shelf did have claws and fast reactions, both evolutionary advantages, but his metal brace was an effective enough bludgeoning tool for me. Soon enough, my hood and clothes were ripped in various places and Shelf's hat and some armor were torn off.
The final blow came when the metal brace smashed its owner's head. Shelf and I paused simultaneously, and soon my opponent fell to the ground, unconscious.

I walked out of the area while roars of applaud and praised rung loudly behind me. The gates were just about to close when I heard a loud series of clicks and hisses. I turned around and played around with the dial until the noises were translated into words.
"Well? What're you waiting for? Get out here!" I followed the voice to see an Omegasect who stood near the top of the bleachers. He was dressed in metal equipment and lots of scientific-looking gear.
"I'm pretty impressed with what you've done here; most everyone is just an all-out brute in these battles! I'll make you a deal. If you can fell one more opponent in this arena, I'll take you onto my ship and out to whatever planet you want!" It was now that I recognized the speaker. He was Gatling, the head space captain on the Omegasect Empire. I heard a lot about him, and looking at the stuff he was equipped with, he certainly was intimidating.
"Well? What do you think?" He called, interrupting my thought. The crowd began chanting "Do it! Do it! Do it!" (Well, the Omegasects were anyway). I stopped to consider the offer. Maybe Gatling could get me back to the Brick-World. Just maybe...

"Deal!" I called back. The crowd roared with excitement.

"And no one noticed him coming in???" Flametorch asked in confusion. He sat with his comrades inside of a medic tent that was set up in Commander GraveBear's military base. MelodyC and Anixian were still recovering from attempted murder from an unknown assailant.
"We've asked guards, checked the security items, everything." Grave assured him. "Nothing showed any trace of this 'Shadowy figure' sneaking into the base."
"And yet somehow he almost got away with a double-murder." Anix mumbled. "At least its over now."
"But what if he comes back?" Melody said almost immediately. There was a pause before there was an answer.
"Look, I'm not sure what happened," Grave started again, "But there's no way he could've gotten past my security protocols. No one has. So far."
"And maybe they found a way." Flame reasoned. "Unlikely, but it's possible, right?"
Melody suddenly felt a harsh shiver run down her spine. Whoa... she thought, That doesn't feel right. There's... some sort of... presence. I'm not sure what it is, but it can't be from the Brick-World...

* * *

"I want that over here." IcyTea told the soldiers as he prepared the base for war. If the spies were correct, there would be an attack happening. A big one. They had to be prepared.

Suddenly a large purple ribbon-shaped tendril appeared, and instantly began wrapping itself around Icy's body.
"What? What the-!?" A second one appeared just as suddenly as the first, and wrapped itself around his eyes. Then the ground beneath his feet vanished, creating a strange zero-gravity feeling. Slowly his vision returned, along with the textures of the world around him.

"Hello." A ghostly figure that sat in front of IcyTea said. "Do you know about this figure named... Daxflame?"
"What the... how... I..." Was the response he got. "Who the heck are you? WHAT the heck are you?"
"ANSWER THE QUESTION!" The phantom snapped.
"Uhh... yes."
"Good. I'd like to have a short talk with you, then."

My eyes refused to open as I sat up in the bed that the Omegasects so kindly offered to me, trying to shake off sleep. After all, today was the day when I had to fight one last "special" opponent in the arena. The best thing about this battle was that even if I lost, could still stay in the Omegasect city and try to find away back to the Brick-World.

A sudden series of clicks made me jump; I was thinking too hard and didn't notice a female Omegasect enter the room with a plate of assorted meats. Quickly I stuck the earpiece to my translator into place and said: "Sorry, what was that?"
"I brought breakfast. The boss of this arena said he wants you ready to fight at seven. We'll let you in the training room until then. Just let us know when you're ready." And with that, she placed the platter onto a dresser near the bed and left the room.
I finished off the bacon, sausage, pork, and steak as quickly as I could and dressed myself in the dark attire that I crashed onto this planet with. It was also a real struggle trying to fit the brace on with only one working arm. Then I knocked heavily on the door to alert the Omegasects that I was ready. Quickly to of them came and led me down to the training room, where I would stay for the next half hour. They then abandoned the area quickly.

The training room's floor was completely made of mats, and there were various things set up for each possible way that a Sporeverse creature could fight. Lined up against one wall there were 3 different wooden manikins, each one with various types of scratch marks and slashes all over. On the opposite wall were similar manikins, though these ones covered in bitemarks and needles. The back wall housed 2 machines that could register the amount of poison that they were hit with, and the effectiveness of said poison would be rated from 1 to 5 on a meter.
Aside from those, there was a large weight set next to the poison machines, and they had a numerous variety of grips, each one for whatever possible hand type a Sporeverse creature could have. And in the very center of the room there was a large punching bag that was suspended from a chain that was screwed into the ceiling.

Wow, a half-hour certainly passed quickly, I thought as I stood at the gate that would soon open up to the arena. The thing that troubled me the most was that I had no idea what kind of creature I would fight against. After all, the tournament was over, wasn't it? Maybe it was a winner of a previous tournament. Or maybe an Omegasect fighter? Either way, I would still survive. Unlike last time, if I lost I would get tossed out of the city and would be at the mercy of planet Stonage. This time, winning would be a little extra help to get me to my destination rather than mandatory for my survival.
"Um, Mr. Flame" An Omegasect called to me from behind, snapping me back to reality. "We're starting in a minute. Get ready." Wow, Mr. Flame sounded weird. Soon enough, the gates opened, and I stepped out into the daylight with the stands packed with various races of Sporeverse creatures. Up in the announcer tower, Gatling stood next to the announcer. And he was also the one who spoke instead.

"So, Dax," He called down through the microphone "What kind of enemy do you think you'll be fighting here tonight?" I hesitated before answering.
"To be honest, I'm not entirely sure. A winner from an arena tournament, maybe?"
"Well, you're in for quite a surprise then!" Gatling chuckled a little, which made me uneasy. "Open the gate!"
The gate behind me shut, and the one on the opposite side of the field opened up, revealing a tremendous, rhino-sized insect that had strange blue and red patterns decorating its body.

The monstrous creature thrashed around in the chains that it was bound by, which were created of some metal that I couldn't identify. Even the 6 Omegasects with the chains in hand had a hard time controlling the beast. It took a few moments before I could identify it.

It was a Beetle Tank. In the older times, Omegasects used them in a way similar to war elephants when battling each other. More recently, Beetle Tanks were mostly used to destroy secret alien spy outposts, or were secretly planted onto an enemy planet. The creatures' destructive nature and alien existence would completely throw off the natural balance of the planet, ultimately resulting in an EcoDisaster crisis, which would distract the foe's government and grant the Omegasects and opportunity to attack.
The thing didn't really look like your basic beetle at all. Like a normal insect, it had 3 body sections. The abdomen was more of a base where the thing's 4 gigantic legs were attached to. The middle section housed the arms and connected the "base" to the head. The head was very large and orb-like, with large, glaring eyes and a 3-part mandible mouth, similar to that of an Omegasect's, but slightly different. The entire body was naturally colored with seemingly random patterns of blue-green and red. A giant crystal-like spike was on its back.

"Alright boys!" Gatling called down, "On three you all let go! Ready? Say it with me guys! One..." The next number came, and three was finally called out. The three Omegasects holding down the massive beast instantly evacuated back into the gate, and I was left alone in the arena with a creature that was capable of destroying an entire city on its own.

A dark figure with a small torso and long, spindly limbs came shambling out of a doorway, holding a square tray in its hands. It's purple eyes tore through the darkness, casting enough light to illuminate its almost featureless face and upper chest area. The Enderman dropped the metal tray onto the ground in front of MelodyC, who was slouched against the pillar she was bound to. Mel was tempted to look at the thing straight in the eyes just to tick it off, (Endermen were angered by being looked at for some reason) but she knew that her captor would have no tolerance for it. After the creature left, Mel looked at the awfully good-looking food, packed together on the small tray. Then she wondered how much of it was poisoned. But the Phan- er - whatever needed her to make himself "whole again", or something like that, so he couldn't afford to kill her. But then again, that doesn't mean that there's not something added to the food, like a weakness serum or truth potion.
Melody pushed the tray aside, leaving it to the dark rat-things that devoured it in only a few moments. She decided not to take the risk until she was absolutely starving to death.

* * *

Blightblade looked over to his head of Mission Control.
"So!?" He demanded, "Where are they now!?"
The Mission Control Reaperspike looked back from his work. "They're near the center of the Galaxy, working around this way."
"Excellent. We'll be ready for them." Blight looked over to one of the workers. "I need to contact the Space Captain. Can you get him for me?" The worker nodded and went down an elevator shaft. Soon enough, the Captain came up through the elevator and approached his leader.
"You called for me? Apparently...."
"I did." Blight stared right into the Captain's solid red eyes. "I believe you're associated with the space captain we're tracking? Gatling of the Omegasects?"
The Reaperspike Captain growled at the mere mention of the name.
Blight continued. "We.... I have a job for you. I have duties to attend to, relations with a foreign group. I can't have him interfering with my work. When Gatling comes within 7 sectors of here, eliminate him."
The Captain grinned. "With pleasure."

Gatling swerved the starship around, then back to the direction we were heading to avoid some missiles shot from a Grox warship.
"So that's how you wanna play it?" Gatling glared straight ahead at the huge, dark-colored spaceship. Then he twisted a knob on his control panel and five gigantic missiles were launched from the bottom of the Omegasector X. The Red missiles flew straight for the giant warship, swerving around to avoid any other targets, exploding when they hit their mark.
You would think that missiles with that power would easily break down a ship of any size, but the huge warship was still going.
"W-what!?" Gatling swerved the ship out of the way to avoid several laser shots. "Those were top-grade Proton Missiles! Hey!"
I looked at him. "What!?"
"Press and hold the purple button!" I looked around the vast control panel until I found the large, round button. I slammed my fist on it.
Suddenly a huge, blue forcefield formed around the ship, keeping it in a giant sphere. The ship continued on, but all enemy attacks were deflected off of it.
"Hit it again!"
I forced my palm onto the round button, and the shield dropped. Gatling fired more Proton Missiles, which dispersed to destroy several unlucky Grox warships. "Again!" I did as told, and the shields went back up.
Gatling spoke frantically, keeping his eye on the giant warship that we were quickly speeding towards. The thing was shaped kinda like 4 Enterprises from Star Trek smashed on top of one another and then welded together. The top and bottom were cones covered in weaponry, and the sides were covered with oddly shaped windows and more turrets. "Alright, we have to go through it!"
I gave him a look that showed him what I thought of his plan. "What!? You mean, the ship? Through that one!?"
Gatling nodded. "The engine's at the center, and it'll take ages to get there with weapons!" Gatling flipped off the shield. "I'll make a hole as best as I can! You turn the shield on right as we go in!" Then he let loose loads of Proton Missiles, laser blasts, and huge green energy pulses. We went inside the dent that Gatling made with his weapons. "NOW!!!" I hit the button right before we would have collided with the wall.
The shield went up, and Gatling stomped on the accelerator. Loads of metallic material scraped off our shield as we drilled through the Warship. we crashed through several hallways, several control rooms, and finally the engine room. Right as Gatling began driving the Omegasector X into the engine, the shield flickered. We were running out of power.

Flametorch felt like he had read through the notebook several times through by the time he felt the jet come to a landing. He was still pretty amazed that Warbad knew how drive one of these things like he'd been piloting his entire life. Flame set the book aside and stood.
"So... where are we anyway?"
Warbad opened the cockpit door, and a ramp to the ground automatically extended from the plane.
"Where do you think?"
Anixian and Flame followed War out of the jet, taking sight of the ruins of ReSPAWN's clan base, which was currently being rebuilt after the massive attack. They moved quickly to the ruins through the hilly terrain, and within 20 minutes they were at the entrance of the once-great building. All around the base, builders standing on scaffolding were setting metal reinforcements to the bricks walls that cranes were setting up, and wrecking balls tore down the unrepairable parts of the charred buildings.
"Flame... you know Dax better than I do. Where's his room?" Warbad said as he peeked into the hole of the wall of a broken building.
"We might not need to find his room..." Flame and Warbad looked into a hole where Anixian was pointing. Under some rubble, red-carpeted stairs led down into a dark underground area.
After a bit of heavy lifting, the hot, sweating trio walked down the stairs. They each grabbed flashlights and flipped them on once they hit the bottom of the long stairway.

Flame swept his flashlight across the room several times before he noticed that the metal door sitting in the center of the room was actually and elevator. "Hey, guys. Come over here." Flame shined his light on the lightless buttons as the other two came to see what was up. Anix tapped the "down" button several times, though everyone knew that the dislocated button wouldn't do much.
The pad that the buttons were on was smashed into the wall, leaving several cords visible and adding a huge hole in the wall as well. The door itself was heavily dented and torn open just enough that Anixian could peek through with his light.
"The elevator's at the bottom of the shaft. Either of you happen to bring a crowbar?"
Warbad looked around at his belt. "Maybe not a crowbar, but... Anix, you might want to move." Anixian did so, and Warbad took a large, red hammer and bashed it against the door several times, praying that no one up on the surface could hear what was going on. He eventually widened the gap just enough that they could individually squeeze through.
Flame poked his head through the hole and looked into the darkness below. "That's a long fall."
War move him out of the way and tossed some of his rope down into the darkness. "Yeah, try not to lose your grip." He then tied the rope to a scrap of metal that was bolted to the wall.

The trio eventually made it all the way down to the elevator, which was set at the bottom floor. It turned out that the rope wasn't quite long enough to reach from the bottom, but they jumped off anyway, thinking they'd figure out a way back up. Flame and Anixian tore the broken emergency door off the top of the elevator and jumped inside, Warbad following close behind.
They all swept the large room with their flashlights before Flametorch found a switch that lit up several fluorescent lights on the ceiling, most of the with the covers broken and/or hanging off, and all but one flickering in a random manner. The dim light from the five lights was barely enough to illuminate the large area.
This seemed to be some sort of grand hall, though it was hard to tell since the place also looked like it was just hit by a tornado. The red carpet was stained with brown and black spots of varying sizes, and several small tables were broken and tossed to the ground. There was a frame for a painting hanging by a single nail above the stairway to the right and the painting over the left stairway had been shredded to pieces all over the carpeted stairs. Diagram posters that covered various areas of the wall that had once described complex electronic designs and machinery were now mere scraps of paper, stuck to the wall with whatever glue had been used to seal them there. The black metal rail on the stairs and on the top of the stairs had been ripped through in several places, as if by some super-powerful wild animal. The dark brick walls had cracked areas, and in some places the bricks had been ripped out entirely, revealing the concrete behind.
The ceiling was basically some structural-supporting metal beams with lots of wires above them. There was rubble that was once dark marble, crafted into pedestals that probably had some sort of interesting item on top.
The team could see four metal doors, each with small flickering lights on the edges: Three on the upper area, and one between the stairs on the floor where the trio stood.
Each member of the group stood in silence, imagining what the place could have possibly been like before the chaos.

Part 3: Evil Revealed

A loud, metallic slamming sound snapped MelodyC out of her almost sleep-like trance. Two more Endermen shambled on their long limbs over to her shackles, removing them carefully, but each one also holding an arm. Mel's thoughts raced, but eventually one question arose: what now? The Endermen forced Mel to her feet and led her to the staircase outside the rusty iron door, which was shut afterwards.
Melody felt like she'd die of starvation and exhaustion after the climb up the long, dark staircase. The next room she entered into with the guards was actually really comfortable-looking, like an overly furnished - and dark and creepy - living room. Unfortunately, the Endermen dragged her through room after room before she could take in each dark and purple scene.

Mel lost track of where she was being taken by the time the Endermen took her down the next stone stairway. This one had tall, chapel-like windows with transparent purple curtains, letting in moonlight from outside. At the bottom of the stairs, the Endermen pushed open wooden double doors, revealing a place of both wonder and nightmare for Mel.

This place was a huge, mostly stone brick chamber in a semicircular shape. Along the rounded side were four tall windows, similar to the ones in the staircase. A wide, stone table stretched alone the flat end of the room, supporting too many magic bottles and other mystical alchemical things to count. The corner of the table also had several darkened bows and twisted and evil looking swords. The circular wall had chains attached, as well as other familiar objects pushed against it - a Minecraftian brewing stand, two large anvils, a few cauldrons with variously colored liquids, and some other things that were unidentifiable. The center of the room had a large stone altar-like table, with some sort of strange instruments hanging above it. An ugly purple and blue-green sat underneath it, and standing adjacent to the table was the ghostly creature himself.

The Endermen left the room quickly, letting go of Mel and slamming and locking the doors behind them, leaving Melody alone with the creepy figure.

"Welcome." The ghost said in his dark, twisted voice. Mel couldn't come up with anything worth saying back, but it turns out she didn't have to. Several wispy tendrils jumped from the floor and encircled Melody, and she screamed for a second before the sound was cut off. She tried to speak, but no sound would come out of Mel's mouth. Her own powers failed as well.
With a movement of his hand, the ghostly spirit raised Mel from the ground, using the magic to drift her over to the central table, dropping her on top of it. Melody tried to roll off, but the magic became concentrated around her arms and legs, trapping her on the table, but releasing her mouth. Looking down, the spirit said, "This won't hurt a bit, I promise. It'll hurt quite a lot. Only for you, though." One of the magical instruments above the table appeared in the "hand" of the wispy figure. One moment later, Melody's screams could be heard all the way throughout the castle.

"Anything yet?" Warbad came out of the higher-right metal door, which miraculously still slid upwards automatically.
"Nope." Anix came out of the left one.
"What about you, Flame?" Warbad said as both he and Anix peered into the upper-central room. The door slid open fully, allowing them to go inside.
"Actually, you guys may want to check this out." Came Flametorch's reply from the darkness. War and Anix approached the small beam from Flame's light which was shown on a wide crack in the wall, revealing some sort of secret room. "Can you two help me with this?"
Using their combined strength, the trio pushed the wall inward, and forced it sideways just enough to squeeze through to the other side. Anixian was the first to step inside, followed by Flametorch and finally Warbad. When War entered the room, he suddenly felt the floor beneath him give way a little, snapping on the only two unbroken lights in the room. The lights revealed a pedestal inside of a smashed glass chamber. Using their flashlights to work their way through the rubble over to it, the trio examined the chamber carefully. Something was connected to some heavy-duty cords in here previously, but had been ripped away by some wild force. Many small scraps of metal were laying on the floor on this area. Anix's flashlight found something sparkling on the ground. He picked up a few of the marine-colored particles. Flame and War looked over Anixian's shoulder.
"Diamonds." He said after analyzing them a bit. "But not from anything we've seen around here."
"You don't think-" Flame's comment was cut short by the sudden appearance of two glowing purple eyes in the darkness. Dark-piercing purple and lavender particles encircled the shape of the creature. Flame recalled Melody talking about things like this - Endermen, she called them. But this didn't seem quite like how she described them. The trio shined their lights on what turned out to be a wispy, muscular body. Not the frail and skinny forms that Melody described.
Suddenly Flametorch collapsed. Warbad and Anixian both shouted his name and instinctively went to help him up. Flame's body seemed almost lifeless, though he was clearly conscious. Anix supported Flametorch by the shoulder while Warbad pulled a pistol from his holster, pointing it against the beast in the dark. Suddenly Flame coughed and dark, almost black blood splattered onto the floor.

"What the heck are you doing!?" I looked at Gatling, who was flipping around some sort of blue-lighted levers that were at the very end of the complex control panel.
"I'm rerouting the power from the weapons to the shield!" Gatling looked forward again, facing the mass amount of scraps and such that were flying past, torn apart by the energy shield. Then he murmured, "We're not gonna have enough..."

Suddenly Gatling rose and sped to the back of the cockpit, tearing the door open and revealing another portion of the red-lighted vessel. "Get over here!" I did as Gatling said. He pulled open yet another metal door, which revealed a closet stocked with barrel-sized cylindrical capsules with green and blue labels on them. Gatling picked one up, clutching it with both of his claws. "The floor!"
I looked down, and saw what Gatling was implying. As quickly as possible, I grabbed a small latch and pulled open a trapdoor in the floor, which was big enough to fit two of the large capsules inside. The interior resembled that of a battery container. Gatling quickly inserted the blue-labeled capsule into on of the sections, snapping it into place. He did the same with a second capsule from the closet, then shoved the closet door and trapdoor shut. He then raced back towards the cockpit with me following close behind. We got back into the captain and passenger seats right as the ship broke through the hardened outside of the giant warship, which gave a good amount of opposition before finally giving in. I could finally take a sigh of relief.
"Glad that's over." I muttered, slouching back in my chair.
"Don't get too comfortable." Gatling said without taking his eyes off of the army in front of us. "Those backup energy capsules won't last us long. If I use the shield or weapons for too long, we won't have the power to escape Grox territory."
"What's stopping us from dropping in another pair?"
"Can you fly this ship through enemy fire?"
"No."
"That's why. We'll be blown to pieces before I can replace the capsules."
"So what do we do?"
"Cross your fingers and hope that I can make it out of here without overusing our power."

* * *

The dark dungeon chamber was quiet, except for the sounds of a small creature scurrying across the floor every now and then and Meldoy's labored breathing. After what the ghostly form did to her, she was thrown back in here and chained up in the same place as before. Two strange pots releasing short-lasting, low-lying purple smoke sat to her sides. These were supposed to allow her power to return more quickly so that the painful process of extracting it could happen again.

After the horrible pain had ended, Mel's vision was blurry, but she could make out a trio of bottles sitting on the table with her. They contained some sort of glowing, gas-like substance. She had then witnessed her captor uncork the top of one. Instantly the lavender substance enveloped his body completely, then vanished mysteriously. He repeated this with the second two. Each time he did this, his form seemed more solid than ghostly. By the time the villain had Melody taken away, his purple form had become darker and more concentrated. One could now vaguely make out four long limbs and a small torso, as well as what might have been eyes.

Melody had no idea how long it would take for her power to return, but she hoped it would be a while. She wasn't ready for another painful extraction process.

Warbad's hand shook as he pointed his Piranha pistol up, straight between the creature's eyes. At the slightest movement, he was ready to let loose with firepower.

The monster moved so quickly that it was unrealistic. The gun was knocked from War's hand before he could take the first shot. Another swift motion knocked him to the floor. Anixian set Flame down, in the corner of the small area which they were in. He then lifted up his own pistol and shot as many times as possible. But, to everyone's astonishment, nothing landed a single hit on the monster. A huge shadowy hand clasped Warbad around the neck and lifted him into the air. Another one sent a straight punch that knocked Anix to the wall, rendering him unconscious. Or dead. War couldn't tell, but he hoped it was the former. Warbad grabbed the light on his belt and flipped it on right in the creature's face. The monster responded violently, throwing War across the room and into a wall. The light now displayed the entire creature dimly.
It had a large, skull-like head with a pair of narrow eyes that shown purple in the dark. It was roughly three times as tall as any of the Brick-men, and had a surprisingly lean form. The torso was small in proportion to the limbs attached to it. The beast had four arms that each ended in large, three-fingered hands. The entire body looked like it was made of perfectly black gas, flowing in an endless current and forming the creature's body.

Warbad worked up his strength to stand up, grabbing the flashlight as well. Normal weapons clearly don't do a thing to this... thing. He thought, ...But light does? War ran to the creature, leaping over rubble when necessary. He pointed the beam at the monsters heart, and watched carefully as the shadowy gas flowed outward to avoid the light. Weird, but he didn't have time to work out a plan. A monstrous hand slammed into him, sending War crashing to the ground and making the flashlight fly across the room before hitting the wall and breaking completely.

Twas the night before Brickmas, and all through the map
Everyone looked like they were taking a nap.
The lobby was filled with chatters galore,
Spamming for account trades, free tokens and more.

The children were all trying to upgrade their stuff.
Trying to link more armor, to become more buff.
I in Defense mode and my friends all in play,
Had been farming XP most of the day.

When out of nowhere St. Brickolaus appeared,
I looked at his profile and he looked pretty geared.
Using the new “join player feature” I jumped to his room,
Joined into game and prepared to spread doom.

When, what to my wondering eyes should appear,
But a miniature backpack with tiny reindeer.
People using items like warpies, running all quick,
I knew in a moment it must be St Brick.

And then, in the chat box I saw someone type
St. Brick has a Mumba and is starting to snipe.
As I tossed some snowballs used reloads and tossed more,
When I turned around St. Brick opened the door.

He was dressed in a Santa suit, upgraded to the max,
And I seen in chat, all the kids calling hacks.
A barrage of bullets flew towards my face,
And grenades were tossed all over the place.

He sprang out of nowhere, crossbow in hand,
Arrows flew sticking into the wall where they land.
But I heard him exclaim, as he ran out of sight,
"Happy Brickmas to all, and to all a good-fight!"
