Hello all. As some of you may know, there was once a story on this forum that I had written about one of my maps, but I took it down to be edited. Now it's edited, and I'll post one part at a time to keep things even. For now, I think one part a day will suffice until I'm at the end. Please note, this story is still a work in progress and the parts that do end up on here are the polished versions.

There were some changes to the plot, grammar and spelling fixes, and getting rid of unnecessary parts of the story.

Feedback is always welcome, and I hope you enjoy!

-MelodyCreeper

Part 1:

It’s been almost three months now since my arrival on the Brick-World and the journey of our platoon. Before that, there were three hours of fleeting travel, followed by an hour of trying to convince a local king to let me join his ever loyal army… I found myself in the hands of a planet and its people I didn’t realize existed until recently.
Now after flying through space once again, landing, getting our gear, and traveling for what seemed like an eternity has brought me and my platoon here. Riding in a smallish army jeep from the last B.L.U.E base we stopped at to restock on supplies for our journey. Our initial objective has been completed; find the R.E.D missile silo and put it out of commission. Now that our platoon, the First-Strike platoon, has no other objectives, we’ve been traveling around New-Brick helping others with their missions. It seems the Brick-Force has found something of interest…
“You look out the window too much,” a voice remarks from my left.
“Oh do I? What if I’m thinking?” I reply; gaze still fixed upon the rolling blocky landscape. The noise around me rises but I ignore it.
The voice rambles on, “Well you’re too quiet. Either looking out there for something, or listening to your music. It’s too loud by the way. I can SEE the actual music coming out from your headphones. How can you even hear what I’m saying?!”
“What do you mean by that? You can see music notes floating from the speakers?” I laugh, “I can hear you...I just can…”
“Yeah? Well I don’t see how…” another voice chimes in from behind.
I laugh; a small secret I share with only myself for now. My gaze is ever fixed upon the roaming dirt; one arm on the window’s edge supporting my incredibly blocky head.
The voice from behind speaks again, “Hey, look guys.”
I let the headphones drop off my head so I can turn around to face the owner of the voice behind me. He’s a brick with an oven’s head and glowing green eyes; wearing the standard issue combat clothes assigned to new soldiers, and a police baton at his side. A trooper helmet is strapped tightly onto his head. He cradles his weapon in his lap.
“What is it Flametorch?” I inquire.
He points to the horizon where a tall sharp-looking structure appears to be growing out of the ground. As the jeep gets closer, the ground appears to rise around it.
I hear other bodies behind me shuffling to get a better look as well. We’re getting closer, and this structure looks...vaguely...familiar.
“LISTEN UP SOLDIERS!”
Almost like programmed robots, all of us turn in our seats to the front of the jeep where Commander Gravebear has jumped up from his seat. Through his shades his eyes appear serious.
“YOU WERE BROUGHT TO THIS NEW DISCOVERY FOR A REASON. R.E.D HAS FOUND OUT ABOUT OUR SECRET HERE! IN FACT THEY’RE ON THEIR WAY RIGHT NOW!” He bellows.
Then he lowers his as if the enemy could be listening at this very second, “What the Brick-Force’s Archaeologists found here is quite amazing…It seems to be ruins of an old castle or garden; however, the structure itself looks fairly new. What we don’t understand is how it got here, seeing that this planet is three years old and only one-fourth of the way complete of forming. This is why it’s so interesting.”
He pauses, “Any questions?”
The brick in front of me speaks first, “yeah…how can you tell that somebody didn’t JUST build this? And who ordered our platoon here in the first place? We’re already on another mission.”
posts.e: Last edited by MelodyC; 25.11.2014 at 21:50. Reason: bold

posts.h:
The commander takes off his shades and studies them, “Well Boopboop, there are CLEAR markings all along the walls that tell us they sure weren’t part of any Brick civilization. And blood...dried blood on the walls. We dated it and it’s fairly old… It’s almost like this structure is forming with New-Brick.”
Whoa wait...blood? And symbols…
He puts his shades back on, then glances up at us. “ Besides, Kubrick asked for this platoon personally.”
We glance at each other nervously. Kubrick must have his reasons. Maybe he thinks we’d know something.
The Commander nods to us then says, “It appears we have arrived.”
Tents are set up all around the structure; supply tents, medical tents: the works. Many of the tents are settled under the trees of a dense forest, while some poke out just in front of the trees. I can’t really see anything else from the angle the jeep was parked at. The commander tells us to get off and grab our gear. I pick up my blue surgeon’s bag and Scarab. The other members of my platoon follow. I let them pass me to get out, and once they do, they stop in front of the door in awe.
“Hey guys, let me through,” I say shoving through them.
“Wo-wow,” flametorch breathes.
My Scarab falls out of my hands. I take a step back while they take a step forward. Their eyes are filled with wonder; mine with fear. They gather everything and calmly move on towards the camp. I remain as still as a statue.
Before me stretches what looks like a combination of a castle AND a garden. Not one or the other. Small pathways are engraved in the hills, some leading up to the tops of the cubish platforms decorated with bushes, flowers, and trees. Amongst the stone walls of the pathways, symbols dart in out of my vision. Moving pictures tell stories that I know too well. Gates and fences block off exits out of the hidden pathways, and an elegant stone wall runs to the right of this garden but it ends abruptly like whatever it was protecting wasn’t there anymore. A tall spear-like tower shoots out of the ground in almost the very middle.
N-no…This isn’t possible…This isn’t supposed to be here.
I’m now shaking and I feel a little faint. If…
That mean’s his troops are on another planet. They’re coming here too soon.
Gingerly, I take a step forward almost reaching the edge of the garden. I take another step. And another. Then finally my right foot finds the stone ground boundary, and a path begins in front of me. I inhale a deep breath and plant my left foot on the stone path. I brace myself in for the oncoming wave of sound that is a calming whoosh of a thousand or more voices.
A warm welcoming gust of wind blows past me and settles down on the tents behind me. The garden lights up with life, the symbols become clearer, the fountain gushes more water, and the atmosphere grows brighter. It looks healthier now.
I whisper so that no one will hear me, “Dromczai pre Nova Spade?”
I’ve claimed it as my own.

Part 2:

“Isn’t zis place interesting?”
What appears to be one of the Brick-Force’s archaeologists comes up next to me. The dusty old jacket he’s wearing blows in the wind, and he’s having a hard time keeping his hat on. He has a shovel in hand and a shining green rock in the other.
“Vee just found zis over by zee stables,” he exclaims proudly.
I tilt my head to the side to get a better look at it.
I abruptly state, “That rock isn’t worth much. At least not money wise.”
He looks puzzled at my remark. “How do you know zat? Vee have never seen a specimen quite like zis before.”
“Well...I-I…” I stutter.
He chuckles, “Oh no worries...I’ll just leave you to vhatever you vhere doing.” He turns and leaves.
So I go through middle pathway that leads to the stable and fountain area, march up the steps to the fountain and through the little gap…
That wasn’t there… Still changing forms I see?
Pausing, I scan the terrain. Behind the broken wall, lie more Brick-Force tents. The forest springs up behind me and a wide field stretches past the broken wall. The outlines of mountains glint faintly in the distance. The tower springs out of the ground right in front me. Taking a deep breath, I chuck my surgeon’s backpack to the top of tower’s peak, sling my Scarab over my shoulder, and begin climbing.
Oh good, the footholds are still here.
A small grin forms on my face as a flood of nostalgic memories overtake me. I’m at the top, and holy cow! The New-Brick landscape looks beautiful from up here. The sun is setting in the sapphire-blue sky and the soldiers are busy chattering about the oncoming attack…
Then I remember: R.E.D is coming because they want this place for themselves.
My nostalgic smile turns into a glare. He’s planning a counterattack; and we’re in the very middle of it...

Part 3:

I’ve been sitting up here for what feels like awhile, just staring down at the vast bricky landscape that surrounds the garden. The sun sinks lower into the horizon and the sky burns orange and red.
A noise from below startles me.
“Hey. How did you get up there?” It says.
I break the trance that I had cast upon myself. “Oh. What?” I turn to the speaker whose soldier name is Boopboop. “I climbed.”
“Climbed?” He ponders skeptically, “Maybe you borrowed a jetpack from somebody. You can’t climb that because the tower is built in such a way that it won’t let you.”
“No I climbed. There’s cracks in the sides. Just, just...nevermind,” I sigh.
“O-kay. Well, they’re serving dinner now. Better get your rations while you can.”
I nod and simply leap off the top; backpack on, and Scarab in hand. Boopboop winces when I hit the ground. I gracefully land on my feet without falling over, then I begin walk away like it was nothing. He remains standing observing the setting sun behind the tower’s long shadow.
“Coming?” I question him.
Boopboop replies, “Oh, yeah. I was just checking out the tower. This place is strange, but it’s interesting at the same time…”
“That it is,” I mumble under my breath.
We walk off towards the tents where intoxicatingly delicious smells fill the air. As we approach, we see soldiers lined up outside a large tent with trays waiting patiently to get their dinner rations. I shoulder my bag and clip the Scarab to the side of it so I won’t have to hold it any longer. We get our trays and wait.

~♫~

After we finally get our food, we join a table with the rest of our platoon. Small talk slowly fills the dining tent making the ambience louder. Everyone looks cheerful and wide-awake. I feel like I’m about to pass out. Claiming the garden has taken a lot of energy out of me. I plop the tray on the table and drop down into the seat. The chatter at my table abruptly stops, but I’m too busy digging into the bean casserole to notice.
“Er, Mel? Why is your food green? And, um, glowing?” Flametorch asks.
I examine it the beans and sigh without a hint of surprise displayed on my face.
“It appears to be so,” I utter drearily.
Boopboop turns to me, “Is something wrong?”
I yawn, “No. Just a little tired is all. Nothing particularly of interest”
“Well...your casserole is GREEN. I’d say that’s something of interest,” Flametorch says.
I’d explain to them, but they wouldn’t believe me and I have an image to maintain here...
“Excuse me young lady,” a voice from behind me chimes. “I could not help but notice that your rations are, well, quite different from everyone elses.”
“And?” I reply.
“Well, I was just wondering if I could take them back to the research tent to be analysed,” he adds with a pleading smile.
“Go nuts.”
“Thank you,” he does a quick bow then makes off with my tray in a flash.
I sit there and watch everyone else eat; prop my head on my arm and stare at their plates. They look a little uncomfortable. So I sigh and put my head down.
Hmm...wait a sec… Not all of our platoon is here…
“Hey guys. Sorry I’m late to the party,” someone behind me apologizes.
I look up just in time to see a dull yellow tray come down from above and set on the table. The noise of a chair scraping back is faintly heard and then being pushed in. I abruptly put my head down again.
“Hey Anixian. I’m guessing they gave you guard duty right as you walked in, huh?” Boopboop says from my right.
Anix replies, “Pretty much. From what I’ve heard, ever since the R.E.D spies were caught, they’ve doubled the guard duty. Heh. Probably a wise decision. Who knows what kind of secrets this place has hidden... ” He pauses. “What’s wrong with Mel?”
Flametorch laughs, “I think she’s mad that a scientist took her food away.”
My head shoots up, “No. I’m tired; that’s all. This place drains the life out of me…” They stare at me questioningly after those last words shoot out of mouth.
“You can have my food. I’m not really hungry,” Anix offers.
I smile and shake my head, “No thanks. It’ll just turn green again.”
With that, I push back my chair, get up, and leave through the waving flaps of the tent. Cold wind blows gently through.
I sprint to the other side of the garden where a large fenced-off pasture lies with a small pond and birch trees. I sigh. This pasture is supposed to be filled with cows, but obviously, cows do not duplicate between planets. I still wish they were here. I climb the fence and deposit my bag next to the nearest birch. Grasping the trunk, I shake the tree until an apricot falls out of its branches. I pick up the fruit which immediately begins to glow a soft green color.
I laugh, “I’ll never understand why you bear apricots, my little tree. I remember when I first planted you.”
The sky is no longer crimson and stars begin emerging from the silky blackness of space. Sitting under the tree, I eat the fruit until there’s nothing left but the seed in the middle. Wind whistles through the branches leaving it’s strange coolness lingering behind. It almost reminds me of winter.

Part 4:

“Melody! Where did you go?” a faraway Anixian shouts.
I get up. “Over here!”
He sprints up some stairs, around a corner, and jumps the fence. “Curfew is, huff, in… twelve minutes,” he pants. “But Commander Gravebear was wondering if you wanted to help guard during the night.”
He seems a bit anxious for an answer.
“That doesn’t make sense,” I answer, “I’m a nurse, not a guard…” My voice trails off.
I look up at the moon. It’s huge and yellow. I recognize this; tomorrow it will be orange. Then blood red the next night. Realization hits me. The reason Kubrick wanted our platoon to come here is because I knew I would recognize this place and have knowledge on it. Gravebear might have an idea that I do as well…
Gravely, I finish my sentence, “I’ll...do it.”
“Ok. Meet us by the tower in ten minutes.” I watch as he jumps the wall, sprinting off to find more guards. A smile that I can’t hide crosses my face.
I look back towards the moon. In two nights time, this garden isn’t going to be fit for the living. Blood moons they say, are deadly.
There’s still time to kill before I’m supposed to meet with the other guards so I decide to check on something. I cross over the little bridge that leads to a towering pine tree, cross another bridge, and down some stairs. Underneath the little island of the towering pine tree is a small chamber outlined in red stone with thick metal bars blocking any trespassers. Through the bars, a small blood red flame dances in the twilight. Words hang scrawled over the door that reads:
“Atar ce Absent-lee. Eire toi gate uneli him woki.”
In an ancient language from another planet it means: “Altar of Darkness. Only enter if HE has awoken.”
Gate’s still closed. That’s good; at least they have the sense not to open something that radiates evil. But still… could HE even be able to come to this world?
After making sure the bars are secure and no damage has been done, I turn my attention to a squared crevice across from the entrance to the altar. The walls are checkered with creamy black and white tiles. The absence of letters surprises me. I blink my eyes several times to make sure I’m not seeing things, but as I get closer, sure enough there are no words. A shudder runs through me as I touch the cold wall.
“Please free us...” The cold wind whispers. Voices form out of gusts of wind; whispering the symbols scrawled all over the stony walls. They sob and shiver, demanding to be released.
I back away, shaking. The voices retreat as I leave; as if they’re taking cautious steps backwards. Once I’m a good enough distance away, I make a break for the tower. Some other guards have already arrived and are looking towards the sky where clouds gather in front of the large yellow moon.
“Looks like it might rain,” one whispers to the other.
The other nods in agreement, “It’s gonna make our job that much harder.
Speaking to myself, I whisper, “I’m going to need a cloak then…” I’m changing my direction when a mini wave of guards comes trudging up the steps followed by Commander Gravebear. Someone shoves a wooly grey cloak into my hands and I hastily put it on, leaving the hood down because I’m wearing a helmet.

Part 5:

The Commander gives us a set of instructions, and positions. Then he gives us our shifts and assigns comrades to each guard. We’ll be guarding in pairs or groups of three at specific points around the ruins. I’m in one of the few groups of three with Anixian, (not a big surprise) and a soldier called Harper. We’re positioned on an island right over a small room outlined in blue stone with the words: “Atar ce Luminee,” carved into the stone. That means “Altar of Light” in the same language as the words over the Dark Altar.

Gravebear hands us each a flashlight, some flares, and a communication device. We’re to guard until the sun rises in the morning. We’re also allowed to take shifts so that some of us may sleep. Then he walks briskly away to attend to other groups.

The first few hours pass with the rain pounding on the bricks and blocky grass. The stars vanish from the sky one by one; as if some unseen force is plucking them away. It seems strange that there are no Fragments falling down from the sky as they enter the new planet’s atmosphere and continue to build this beautiful landscape. I miss seeing the rainbow colors softly streak through the sky every night. We sit silently, guns at our sides incase we have to use them.
Midnight comes and the rain stops abruptly as the time enters a new hour. The clouds part suddenly leaving the large yellow moon hanging in the sky. No stars twinkle. From our position, we can see the whole garden illuminated in an unsettling glow.

“What in Kubrick’s name is happening…” Anixian gets up to observe the changing atmosphere. “It’s almost as if the weather is bended differently around this place.”

Harper and I stand next to him. Glancing around the garden, I notice other guards getting up from their posts and examining the unsettling change in weather.

Shadows begin to bend in odd shapes and a low hum is heard. It’s deep and throaty. Symbols on the walls begin to glow; but only specific ones, meaning that they’re warning of something. I wrap the wool cloak tight around me as the strange winter-like breeze has picked up again. A dark fog rolls in.

In the distance, the fog clusters around silhouettes of other guards. It settles over them for a moment and then darts away, leaving the guard lying on the ground.This is the work of sleeping magic.

“Oh-ho-kay…” Harper breathes in fear. “Um, I think I’m gonna go now…” He leaps over the the wall making a break for the tents.

Anixian and I watch his shadow get smaller and smaller.

“Coward,” Anixian whispers. We turn to see the clouds of black fog getting closer; snaking their way up towards us.
Perhaps a little bit too calmly Anixian says, “So. What do we do about this?”

“We? I do believe you mean, ‘you,’” a deep male voice chuckles.

The fog rushes towards Anixian, knocking both of us over. I fall into the soft grass, sitting up just in time to see the cloud ascend.

Shadows and the remainder of the clouds swirl in front of me until a towering dark figure with glowing white eyes is gazing down at me.

“Pardon me for sweeping past you, child. I’m equally sorry for putting your,” he hesitates, “friends, to sleep. This was the only way I could talk to you.” The word “friends” hisses from him as if it’s painful to say.
The shadow offers a silky black tentacle to help me up. Timidly, I grip it pulling myself up in front of him.

Stuff happened.
Game is dead.
Must find new friends.
All will be my friend.
I need to become...friendlier...

Part 6:

I brush bits of grass off me, “Thanks. But, how’d you know I was here. More importantly, how’d you get here?”
“Simple. I waited until Nova Spade appeared here. Then I went through a gate. However, my form is very unstable, as you can see, I am merely a shadow.”
Eagerly I ask, “You went through a gate in one of…What’s it like there? Are they still upheld?”
The shadow sighs, “I’m afraid the Craftian Gate is overridden with his forces… So I went through the Little Gate. I’m sorry my dear, but they’re getting closer.”
“The Little Gate doing any better?” I sigh.
He shakes his head, “No. They are having problems with spastic attacks from the portal and the weather is severe. It’s winter in summer right now.”
I study the shadow looming over me, “We don’t have much time then.”
“Indeed. Back to more important matters. My dear, I came to warn you,” he stoops down as if to whisper to me. “I assume you are aware the blood moon happens in two nights, yes?”
I nod swiftly; a shudder runs through me.
“Well then...you know not to be awake when it occurs,” his glowing eyes glare towards the sleeping guards.
I go pale, “O-of course.”
“I would have you resume a Collection, but considering your current state...I’d be wise not to…”
My eyes wander away from him and into the darkness of the night. Towards all the unconscious soldiers, and Anixian who lies in a heap right underneath a tree. The fog gets heavier and swirls with a slow spiraling motion.
Another tentacle appears and touches me lightly under my chin making me look up into the shadow’s cold eyes, “Do not. Wake up. Or be prepared to make a sacrifice. You are still too young to control corruption, my dear.”
He lifts the tentacle and it dissolves into the night air. “Now I’m going to put you to sleep as well,” a hint of playfulness fills his dark voice, “It’ll make you look less suspicious.”
I simply nod again. In one swift movement he veers the inky fog at me. My legs begin to shake and the world slowly tips back and forth. Eyelids slowly getting heavier, I fall over. I feel the shadow catch me before I hit the ground, then gently set me down. I dream of a steady stream of water flowing from behind a crack. .

Burgers.

Part 7:

Waking up with a pounding head and an aching back isn’t fun.
“Ugh,” I wince as I sit up. The sun is halfway at its peak and there’s not much noise coming from the tents. I check out my surroundings. A few guards still lay fast asleep in the grass or sprawled out on the stone pathways. Anixian doesn’t appear to be anywhere in sight, so I’m guessing he must have woken up or got moved.
The waterfall.
I shoot up from the ground. The waterfall! Of course! And behind the waterfall is…!
Wait. How is this going to work… I don’t want to raise suspicion. Ever since I joined the Brick-Force, they have all had the feeling that I wasn’t an average Brick-Person. I can’t tell them the truth because it risks the safety of this planet.
After thinking it through, I decide to access it in plain daylight. But not at this moment. My stomach rumbles. Glancing at the sun again makes my hunger roar even louder. It’s almost noon.
“Great. I suppose another apricot will have to suffice?” I complain to myself.
Walking back to the fenced off area of trees, I examine all the sleeping guards. Some of them fell asleep in weird stances; standing or sprawled out over a block. There’s even a few who are sleeping on their heads. This makes me giggle; I knew he had a sick sense of humor, but I didn’t know that he used it to possibly entertain me. I clamber up the same tree as yesterday and grab the biggest fruit I find.
“Hey there!”
I fall out of tree in surprise, “ANIX! Don’t scare me like that!”
He snickers, “Haha! Should’ve seen the look on your face.” He helps me up, then clears his throat, “Anywho, I’ve been wandering around the ruins, and well, there’s only a couple of other bricks awake. Everyone back at camp is fine but they’re too scared to come over here and check everything out, and…” His sudden stop worries me.
“What?”
“What...is that black mark on your forehead?” He questions while looking at me suspiciously.
I exclaim, “What?!”
I dart across the courtyard of the tower to an elegant bubbling fountain. Sure enough in my reflection, there’s a black slash across my forehead. My cheeks burn rosey red.
“What...does that mean…” Anixian questions from behind.
I don’t answer him but instead a puzzled sound leaves my mouth, “H-he…” I pause. The redness continues to grow on my face. Without saying another word, I rinse the black off my forehead as Anixian watches from behind me; his eyebrows raised in question.
Anixian wheels around, “We should wake everyone up. The sun’s going down faster than in the freezing Brick-World!”
“Of course,” I answer softly. I’ve successfully managed to rub the black off my forehead.
We scout around the garden waking everyone from the dreamless slumber the dark shadow had left us with. Like Anixian had said, there were a few bricks who had woken, but most of them sit dazed in place as if they had no idea where or who they are. Just when we think that there are no more guards to wake up, Anix spots a blue lump hunched over in the bushes.
“Excuse me, but I do believe it’s past twelve now,” he shakes the guard.
The guard’s head turns so fast, Anixian and I leap back in surprise. The sight of the SWAT mask he’s wearing startles us more. “I KNOW THANKS! Does it kill me to get more sleep? I mean, come on! Five more minutes,” he grumbles.
A quick flash of the rank sewn on his jacket makes up our minds. “Yes sir,” we say in unison, backing away slowly. Thankfully, activity has slowly resumed in the garden.
“Now what?” I inquire.
He tentatively replies, “ I guess we get ready for tomorrow.”
I watch him walk down towards the tents; shouldering his gun nervously as if he might need to
use it any second..
These poor people don’t know what they’re getting themselves into.
Thank you, boopboop. ^^

Part 10

I wake up in a cot of the medic tent with aches along my back and legs. No one’s here. And it’s unnaturally dark out.
Where is everyone...And how long have I been asleep? Has it really been a whole day?
A thought hits me.
Oh my Creator...Could it be the same night as…
I get up ignoring the pain and stumble over to the closed tent flap, carefully peeling it open.Wind cuts through the flap like a knife, almost knocking me over.. The moon is full, and it’s blood red. No stars shine and the marked profile of the tower sits dead center in front of the moon. I swear I see whispers hanging in the air.
“No…” I whimper, shrinking back into the folds of the tent.
When? And how?
Shakily, I raise a hand to my face and trace an almost invisible scar that slices into my upper lip. My skin is cold and clammy. Black tears begin to spurt out of my eyes again. A faint humming resonates in the distance.
“NO!” I shout. I have to warn them…
I break out of the tent in a sprint to where I know the shadow left everyone, but its too late. The darkness has found me. They swarm all over the walls and underneath my feet as I run, trying to trip me.
It’s time it’s time it’s time it’s time, they whisper to me.
Feed us, Melody.
“HEY!” I scream, “Everyone needs to leave NOW!” I wave my arms over my head which is hard to do when you have a big blocky head and your arms feel like they’re being pinned down at your sides. “Leave before it’s too late!”
Anix is the first to spot me.
“Mel?” He cries, “What are you doing? Go back to the tents!”
“NO! You need to get out of here!” I screech back. Something moves across my leg right as I move forward to take the next step and I fall to the ground with a thud. Dreadful music. It begins to drag me away.
They leap over the wall to try and reach me. I can’t fight it anymore, so I let the darkness drag me across the stone. I shut my eyes.
Words sickly come out of my mouth, “Don’t follow me. Just...leave…” Every word I manage to sputter out is almost thrown back into my throat.
“Listen to me!” I cry. Tears stream down my face. “I’m not important! You need to go. LEAVE BEFORE YOU’RE ALL TRAPPED.”
Through the dusty moonlight, the boy I saw earlier regards me with pain in his eyes. It’s as if I said something that hurt him.
There’s a spot. That spot. In the wall, where the Altar of Darkness sits. That’s where they take me. While it happens, a corner room outlined in black and white begins to show its lost words. Those three names.
I can never stop what’s about to happen.
At least…not yet…

Nick’s Point of View

The darkness engulfs her and drags her through the barred gates of the Altar of Darkness. The shadow took her, so how many more of us will it take before the night is over?
No one will leave the garden until all corruption is purged… I’ve heard that somewhere before, but I don’t know where…
And those words that she said as she was being dragged away, “I’m not important!” I felt like a stake had been driven through my heart. But I guess now that feeling is gone off because I know she means too well. Both of us are hiding and running from something bigger. And that something is slowly engulfing everything…
“Nick,” StarCloud says behind me. “Grab your Mosquito, we have to get going.”
“Yes sir,” I mumble. How clever I am for using my real name as my soldier name. I wish I picked something more badass.
I look around. Gravebear gives orders to platoons, “We might as well make use of this time and see what we kind find out about this place. I want search parties going everywhere. Obviously this place is more than it seems.”
The Commander motions for us to split up into groups based around our platoons, so I’m with Daxflame, Star, FastDasher, and Delilahrose, (the most annoying creature on two legs). We’re about to get going when someone screams from the tunnel under the tower. Anixian’s platoon which is made up of Boopboop, Flametorch, (missing Melody), Tomlotr and Luzoto, (both got asked to remain behind at Base 5 for repairs), follows ours towards the tunnel. I know it’s a little weird I know almost everything about their platoon, but I do for a reason. We rush down there and the whole tunnel is illuminated in sickly yellow light. It beams stronger over a doorway boarded up with wooden planks. There’s no one here.
“Ok… Someone was obviously down here, and now they’re gone,” Anixian says.
Star shrugs, “That, or the screaming we heard wasn’t real. It was made up by that...thing…”
“It was real alright…” a panicked voice says from the boarded up doorway. We move closer and FastDasher shines the flashlight on another group of bricks. They wince at the light.
“A bunch of shadow-like figures came and took our platoon leader, Warbad,” another one whispers.
Anix frowns, “where’d they go?”
One of the soldiers points to a small doorway to the left of a wooden ladder. It was once boarded up, but the boards are scattered around the floor like something in a rush burst through them.
I shine a flashlight into the doorway, casting light on an endless set of stairs that seem to crawl straight down into eternity.
Then of course she has to open her mouth, ““I’m NOT going down there! Too dark…and weird looking...”
From the corner of my eye, I see others glancing at her in annoyance; Fastdasher especially. He looks like he’s ready to shove her down those stairs at any second.
I’m the first to speak, “Okay. You can stay up here and let IT take you.” I whisper to Dasher, “It’s fine by me anyways.” We both try to hold in our laughter as we make the dark descent.

“How long do you think we’ve been going down?” Flametorch asks after a while.
“Hard to say,” Anixian answers in sort of a mumble.
It’s true. It feels like we’ve been going down for hours. The passage is narrow and the stairs are steep, so we have to keep a decent amount of space between each other. From out of the corner of my eye a faint light glows. I glance towards it, stopping on the stairs. Sure enough, a small passage to the left leads into a candle-lit chamber with a stone and dirt ceiling.
I motion everyone over, “Guys, this way!” I start down the corridor in a slow sprint.
The room is a cavern, and there are other passageways leading to the right and left. The candles sit carefully placed on rocks in front of a massive wall with some sort of mural painted on it. Red paint makes up a doll-like figure standing triumphantly on a mountaintop. The only face features he has are two glowing white eyes and his sinister grin. He clutches a Dream Orb in a crushing grip; his smile is crookedly scratched across his face. Below him stand similarly shaped people drawn with brown paint; expressions of pain and sadness on their faces. They watch in horror as he crushes the matter that makes up their world.
“What in Kubricks name…” I hear Star breath behind me.
“Hey…” Another voice chimes. Anix rushes up to the mural and points to the Dream Orb. “That looks like a Fragment…”
A sound comes from the corridor on the right and we all jump in surprise. It sounds like the sobbing of a small child.
“Should we check it out?” I ask gingerly.
Star and Anix sigh.
“It’s better than not knowing whatever that thing is,” Star says.
“Hang on,” Anixian says abruptly, “If there’s two corridors, shouldn’t we split up?”
Star answers, “I suppose… I’ll take my platoon down to the left, and you can take yours to the right.”
We nod in unison.
“Signal us if anything happens,” Star adds quickly.

Dream orbs or Fragments, (the name depends on what part of the galaxy you’re in), are pieces of human imagination that form the planets in this galaxy. They are generally pieces of daydreams or brief imaginative thoughts humans have. They are small and delicate and can be manipulated easily by negative forces. When a planet forms out of Fragments like New-Brick, it takes years to finish. Then, when a planet or another celestial object dies, the same thing happens; it breaks up into Fragments which either clusters into the Archive Belt of the Imaginosphere or is recycled to new planets.. That is what’s happening to the sun in the ancient solar system in which their old planet is located.

So Star takes our platoon down to the right, towards the sound. Along the way we pass pictures on the walls. They’re all beautifully painted, and each one depicts a different story in one picture, or at least, another part of the story. As we run, the sound becomes more clear. It definitely sounds like heavy sobs of a little girl. We turn sharp corners and run down slopes. Stalagmites hang from the ceiling along with crimson red crystals. I think I see other corridors leading off in different directions but I ignore them. The sobs get closer. We halt. A huge circular chamber outlined in dark stone sits like a compass in the middle of everything. Different colored lines of light glow from the center and stretch out like spindles onto the walls. Four colored lines are lit: one is a bloody red color, one a sapphire blue, one a soft shade of purple and the last glows emerald green. The green, blue, and purple lines are cracked and streaked with lines of black. The red one pulses with a harsh, evil energy. A vat-like object takes up the very center of the chamber; a jarring white glow resonates from it.
My head suddenly pounds in pain. For an instant in front of me, I see a girl gripping my arm and pulling me along, telling me to hurry.
“The Reactor…” I whisper.
My platoon stares at me.
“The what?” Star questions.
I stutter not sure where that even came from, “The...the Reactor. That’s what the vat-like thing is…”.
It’s almost like I had just remembered something I had forgotten.
“How do you know?” Dax says from behind.
I stare at it, trying to trigger more memories. Nothing crosses my mind.
“I-I don’t know where that came from. It’s like I have memories of this place…” I whisper again.
Star puts a hand on my shoulder, “If you remember anything at all, please tell us. It might be of use. I’m sorry you’re confused right now…”
We stand in silence for a bit staring at this all too familiar room…
...Well, familiar to me...somehow...

“Ok, well there’s a bunch of different corridors leading off in different directions. Where should we look?” Star questions us.
We pick a corridor with the sapphire blue line on the dusty ground running up to it. A sudden thought hits me, “What happened to the sound?”
Everyone halts. We listen but there is dead silence. We start walking again when a faint rumble resonates behind us.
“What sound?” a voice hisses from above.
Looking up, we see the shadow hanging upside down from the ceiling of the chamber like a huge monstrous bat ready to strike. Its two ghoulish eyes stare down in amusement at us. Instead of wings, those tendrils shoot out from its back in that rhythmical dance.
We aim our guns at it. She stifles a laugh as she plunges to the floor. Somehow, she rotates in the air landing with a bow on two delicate legs, the tendrils sprawled out behind her in symmetrical fashion.
You have no idea how long I’ve been watching you,” she chuckles. “Well… I suppose I should welcome you to my quiet corner of light and despair. Welcome to my cave.”
“What did you do with Harper, and Melody? And who knows what you’ve done with anyone else!” Star demands.
The shadow appears taken back for a second then humor fills her eyes again, “Getting right to the point, are we?” She paces back and forth anxiously much like she did on the surface near the tower.
“They’re fine, for now...but I don’t guarantee their safety.” her eyes light up brighter as if she shared some private joke with herself. The pacing continues; showing complete disregard towards our loaded weapons. She merely stares at each one of us one by one as she walks by.
Then she regards Delila with cold eyes. “That one, you shouldn’t trust,” she says very matter-of-factly.
Delila recoils in surprise, her eyes filled with fear.
“What, do you think this is a game?” Star shouts. I can tell he really just wants to unleash hell upon the shadow.
“You have no idea…” comes a snarky reply. The shadow continues her pacing; apparently waiting for something to happen.
There’s a sudden shout in the distance. The sound pierces our ears. The shadow abruptly stops her pacing, staring cooly in the direction of the sound.
A grin forms in her voice. “Well I must be off then,” She says turning her head very slowly in our direction. This time there is a smile; a crooked white one that takes up almost the entire space of her head.
However, I can’t tell whether a look of triumph or pain has crossed her darkened face.
What is it that has begun? A harvest? A cleansing? I wish I could remember!
A faint breeze picks up and the shadow disintegrates completely. The air smells of decay and strangely, roses and apricots...

Part 11:

Star insisted that we try to find where the noise was coming from.
He interrupts the silence, “She was trying to play with our minds. Did anyone else feel like something was probing your thoughts?
“No…” I look up startled at them.
They glance at me with concern for a second, but it passes.
Delila looks like she’s going to run someone through.
“You ok?” Dasher asks her.
She screams at him, “NO! That thing is disgusting! Shoot it next time you see it! Someone shoot it! SOMEONE!”
I have to yell over her, “JEEZ ALRIGHT! But I think it’d be wise to ask her a few more questions. I for one, want to know what’s going on in this strange place. I know I remember something about it...Maybe if we learn more I can get my memories back. Besides, why can’t you shoot her?”
“Be-cause, I don’t like wasting things.”
I swear when we get out of this, the first thing I’m going to do is make her life miserable.
You won’t have to.
I freeze up. The shadow’s voice weaves through my head.
Does it frighten you that I can talk to you, my friend?
My surroundings suddenly look wobbly. Why are you doing this?
...There’s pain in healing sometimes...
“Something wrong, Nick?” Dasher asks me.
I stutter and keep walking, “N-no. N-nothing. Let’s just go.”

~♫~

Both of our platoons have met up again in a tunnel carved out by on odd hilly terrain. We hadn’t found anything but more tunnels; some of them sealed, pitch black, or lit with torches. We chose not to traverse down the ones that didn’t seem to let light in. But who knows… someone might be waiting down there for help.
“Ok, besides not finding anything, did anyone experience something...weird?” Anixian asks our platoon.
Almost all of us nod. But I can’t seem to as my head feels like it’s made out of stone at the moment. Something’s been filling my head with strange thoughts and voices. But none of those are the memories I’ve been yearning for ever since the first flash-back.
Star adds, “The shadow appeared to us in the large room. Nick had a name for it...the...Reactor Room…”
They’re all staring at me.
“Anyways,” he starts again, “Did you go through there?”
“No, but we could see it from the tunnels we did take. We thought we might check it last. But this was weird; before we bumped into you guys, we went past an entrance to that room and it was blocked…” Anixian says with concern.
“FORGIVE ME PLEASE!”
Everyone locks up, glancing at each other anxiously.
“What...was that?” flametorch asks, his voice slightly shaking.
I must be hearing things, because that sounded like Melody. But if she’s near-by, then that means the others that went missing could be as well.
I’m about to explain exactly that to my comrades when the loudest sound that I’ve ever heard explodes from behind us. I do believe each of us are at least five feet from where we were last standing. My heart’s beating in my chest about ten times fast. What was that sound? It sounded like an odd combo of a peaceful song mixed with one of decay and endings. Something beautiful followed by something sinister. Suddenly, another memory pulses through my mind. I grip my head, falling to the floor in pain.
There’s a taller man, surrounded by shadowy figures. They all glare at me. “You aren’t supposed to be here.” He hisses.

It passes, and I sit up. One by one, I glance into the faces of my comrades. Most of them have a different expression on their faces; Dasher’s is one of confusion, Delila’s is one of a frantic worry, all of Anixian’s platoon looks sad and worried, and Daxflame and Star are both still wearing masks.
I immediately ask them something because I have a feeling we all heard different sounds, “What did you guys hear?”
Boop and Flame speak at exactly the same moment, “Someone crying for help.” Anix nods in agreement with them.
“I heard an explosion,” Dasher says, the confused expression still played across his face.
“It sounded more like a loud exhale of air,” Star and Dax say one after the other.
Delila looks very uncomfortable. “I-I...I heard a laugh and a- something...else,” she says in almost a whisper.
I wonder what my face must look like because they look a little concerned towards me.
I think I’m smiling.
And I think I know why.
“What exactly did you hear?” Anix questions me.
I exhale slowly, “Something familiar.”

~♫~

“Anyone remember where we came in?” Dasher says nervously.
A simple shrug from Star and Anix.
“Great…” Flametorch says. It’s been awhile since he and Boopboop have said anything. I wonder if there’s something bothering them.
We came in from a narrow corridor and into a room that looked like some sort chamber with an altar.
Footsteps sound from the far end of the chamber, as they get closer, we raise our weapons. A shadow soon stretches across the floor pointed in out direction. It’s made out of a dim light that pulses down the corridor so it seems to flicker. Soon a figure forms out of the strange dark fog which seems prevalent down here. My finger is resting on the trigger of my mosquito.
“I wouldn’t shoot if I were you,” comes a voice. The figure stops. There’s the harsh flick of a match being stuck and then blinding yellow light. The figure firmly grips a lantern in its left hand.
“M-Melody?” someone says, confused.
She smiles curtly, slowly trudging towards us. The light from the lantern makes her look pale.
“How’d the rest of you get down here?” She mumbles, a strange look on her face.
Anixian answers her gently, “We found our way down here all together based on directions given to us by another platoon. Are you okay?”
She shivers, “I’m….fine….I just…”
She looks away shyly. There’s a sort of pain in her eyes.. “It’s...nothing…”
“Are you sure?” Anixian asks again.
All she does is nod.
0-0, you got some effort put into here. No offence, but I'm lazy, can't be bothered to read all of this though, but effort rating is: 10/10

“And what brings you here, living one?” one of the shadows says in a gruff voice. None of the shadows turn around so it’s almost impossible to tell which one spoke.
Dax swallows. He didn’t think they would hear him. Anix and Dasher inhale anxiously from behind him.
“I-I…. um, we found this passage and decided to explore,” Dax stutters.
Anix approaches nervously, saying, “No! I mean… it was his idea but… Arg, we won’t disturb you any longer. You’re obviously busy.”
“Nonsense,” the voice answers. One of the shadows faces them. He is extremely small; about 4 centimeters tall off the ground and doll shaped: a large round head and a small torso. Like all the others, he is solid black with wisps of Warp coming off his form and two glowing white eyes in the middle of his head.
“Since you have found this place, we will spare you the calamity of being checked for negativity in the complicated way,” he whispers.
“W-what?” Dax asks.
The shadow lets out a sigh, jumping up onto Dax’s shoulder.
He demands to Dax, “Take your mask off.”
“Um… why?”
“Just do it.”
Shaking, Dax removes his mask and tosses it to the ground in front of him.
The tiny shadow nods, “Good, now hold still. I’m going to spread Warp on your forehead. It might sting a little.”
“Warp?” Dasher questions, finally emerging from the darkness.
“Yes, Warp. The substance we are covered in. It determines what is corrupted right now and what is not. If it stays solid black, it means corruption.”
The shadow rubs two of his tiny fingers together until a sticky substance continuously forms as he pulls his fingers apart. Reaching up, he makes two quick movements across Daxflame’s forehead leaving two black streaks. Dax grimaces as the Warp stings his skin. Seconds later, the streaks begin to glow a warm shade of emerald green.
“You have passed,” the shadow says without amusement.
He leaps from Dax’s shoulder onto the ground.
“As for your companions…”
The shadow repeats his process with both Anixian and FastDasher. The streaks on their foreheads both glow green.
The shadow lets out an exasperated sigh, “More positives… We will never find the last negative roaming around the garden…At least you three are safe from any harm as long as you keep your foreheads visible to any shadows, including our mistress-”
“Hold on,” Anix interrupts, “you mean you guys actually are looking for somebody?”
A glare forms on the small shadow’s face, “Yes… And until we purge all corruption, no one leaves. We need one more traitor.”
The trio glance at each other in worry.

Anixian is hesitant to say it, “Is there anything we can do to help?”
The shadow studies the three soldiers carefully as if he doesn’t exactly trust them. He finally murmurs, “You want to help us? None of the living have ever wanted to help us, except for her…”
“Her?” Anixian questions.
“Our mistress,” the shadow sighs. “She is not one of us, but the changes of the moon do affect her as she looks like a shadow right now. She keeps the garden and makes sure the process goes through smoothly. Her mentor calls it a… Collection. On any normal night, she is gentle and kind, but she becomes corrupted along with the garden during a Blood Moon. The state of the Garden is reflected onto her.”
They ponder for a while, until Dax finally asks, “And you said she won’t harm us if we have the markings visible?”
He nods solemnly. “She will recognize you as cleared and not more traitors. But as of right now, there’s no telling what she might do. Even if she does recognize you… There’s something strange going on.”
“Not like any of this is already strange enough…” Dax mutters.
The shadow raises an eyebrow at him, “Stranger than usual. You living ones have never even experienced a Collection before.”
“About us helping you,” Anix says confidently, “as we can, how do we find this, traitor? I’m not sure if you know this, but finding whoever this is will be beneficial to us both. The “Collection” will be completed and we won’t have to worry about any more spies.”
Eventually, the shadow nods in agreement. He leads the trio over to a well they hadn’t noticed on the far side of the chamber behind more crystals. He commands Anix to reach in and grab three stones. Anix reaches into the well, wincing when he touches a cool wet substance, yet he continues and purges deeper. Feeling around, he grasps three stones and pulls them out, handing one to Dax and one to Dasher. Each stone is a cool grey color with a perfectly round hole in the center.
“I don’t know how much these will help you. We shadows have tried to use them to identify traitors but they don’t work well. We may only use our Warp and sometimes not even that is completely accurate. She usually knows who the traitors are but we don’t know her current location, and for some reason she’s having trouble sensing the last one,” he says diligently.
Anixian holds it up to his eye, scanning the room. Through it, he sees the bodies of the shadows as being pure black, and the ones of the marked soldiers as glowing green.
“The traitor will be red when gazed through that stone and our mistress will appear as black with wisps of green. Her essence,” the shadow sighs.
He says with finality, “Now go. You don’t have much time. She’s becoming agitated. There’s no telling what might happen if you run into her. We must find the last one!”
All the shadows in the room turn their heads slowly towards the three soldiers. They blink sadly and nod, as if thanking them for their help. With a flash of dim light, they’re all gone leaving Anixian, Dasher, and Daxflame standing in the middle of a dark chamber, with resting bodies in the corner.
SERIOUSLY WHO READS THIS? D:

posts.h:
Anixian and his company race down the halls towards the Reactor chamber, stone rings clutched in their grasps. Along their way, they pass many shadows who regard them coolly as if recognizing their new role in helping find the traitor. Once they reach the ominous chamber, they halt for a breath.
“Ok…” Daxflame breaths. “We need to do this quickly and systematically. This… traitor could honestly be anywhere.”
Dasher nods in agreement, “Would it help if we split up?”
“No, who knows what might happen if we were cornered alone,” Anixian remarks. “The traitor could recognize that we’re there to deal with them.”
“Together it is then,” Dax replies.

~♫~

StarCloud, Boopboop and I are followed by the happy chatter of the little girl, Cari. As we’ve been wandering around aimlessly, she talks about the moon phases. Almost proudly as if this “Seis” has taught her wisely. So far anything she says doesn’t trigger any memories I might of had about this place.
“The Blood Moon is scary...I don’t usually come out because Seis doesn’t want me to. She says it’s dangerous and after the time he got me-”
“Oh I love Blue Moons! I remember the last time, there was a garden party. Seis let all the shadows out to play under the moonlight and she sat with the other Keepers-”
“Yellow Moons are interesting…the whole garden seems to hum...scary. I’ve heard he comes out a-”
“-but my favorite has to be the Green Moon because of how everything glows in an “ethereal” light. I don’t know what that means but Seis used it and she said-”
Boopboop lets out a sigh; he’s had to put up with Cari’s noise the most as she clutches his sleeve, constantly tugging and chattering in his ear.
He finally stops abruptly turning to her, “Cari… Is any of this really important?”
She looks at him in confusion, “Well… yes. The shadows told me the color of the moon tells you if a Keeper is happy or sad...or mad… They’re great teachers. Have we found Seis yet?”
I shake my head at the little girl. “No Cari… I’m not sure we know exactly where to look.”
“Where exactly are we right now?” Star mumbles.

Silence. We glance around our surroundings and suddenly I notice something familiar. Somehow, we’ve ended up back at where we first came in. The strange mural with the sad people cowering under the red figure sits before us outlined by candles. A whoosh of cold wind blows the candles out, leaving us in more darkness.
I clutch my Mosquito carefully; something seems to be right behind us.
Star produces a flashlight out of a pocket, shining it into the darkness. He swings the light around until it lands on a shadow. This shadow stands perfectly still in an entrance to this chamber and it eyes us suspiciously.
Cari ducks behind Boop in fright.
“And just what do you think you’re doing with the garden’s child, living ones?” it hisses in a familiar voice.
A happy shriek comes from Cari, “Séis! I thought we’d never find you!”
She rushes out from behind Boop, tackling the shadow in a hug. For an instance, I see a happy yet worried expression in the shadow’s eyes.
“Why aren’t you in the Night-zone, Cari?” she says lightly yet with a tone of discipline.
Cari stops, looking at the ground with terror, “H-he… came and I… ran away.”
Séis spreads her tendrils with anticipation, “You did the right thing…”
She glares back at us, “And you… found her…”
“Yes… well she found us more or less,” I say bravely.
She regards me in particular, squinting those glowing eyes. Hesitantly, she approaches me leaving Cari behind her. Star and Boop raise their weapons cautiously and back up. My feet seem to be glued to the floor.
“You…” she whispers in my face, “You seem familiar… just by the sound of your voice. I can tell I’ve heard it somewhere before…”
The memories that have come back to me flash through my mind.
I stammer, “I-I don’t know… I feel like I’ve been here before but… but…”
Her angry expression immediately melts into pain. She studies me sadly, “I remember now...What are you even doing on this planet?”
I open my mouth but no words come out. Suddenly I’m on the floor with my back up against the wall.
The echo of two triggers being held makes the silence seem more deadly. Séis stands just in front of me. Her tendrils are poised in a strike position and there’s pain in her eyes.
“You… you could of gotten yourself KILLED by coming here!” she cries.
In flash of light, another memory pulses through my mind. There’s loud ringing and the room sways. She looks at me with her head tilted sideways.
Static trickles into my vision.

The memory becomes more clear.
I’m sitting in this same garden, but I’m on the surface and looking towards the fountain. This world is familiar; instead of being made from harsh angles and blocky structures, everything is curved and shaped naturally. There’s an elegance to it. The sun seems to be setting in the distance. A noise from my right startles me and I look over. The same girl that appeared in my memory before stands next to me in worry. She looks like sort of a cloth doll; creamy colored cloth skin with a very round head, large blue button eyes framed with thick lashes, and long brown hair that looks like it’s made of a soft yarn. A sack-girl. She tugs on my sleeve and I get up.
“There isn’t much time… you need to leave,” she says urgently.
Words are automatic. “Why? What’s happening?” I answer.
She shakes her head and looks down sadly, “I… you… you don’t want to know. Please go before something happens.”
Light flashes before my eyes and the memory fades. For a split second I see a gate being closed.
The static stops; my vision slowly inches into focus.
Séis still remains over me with her head tilted. Her tendrils have disappeared and she has her arms folded. She looks like she’s about to burst into tears from the way her glowing eyes seem to waiver.
I stare back in confusion and wonder.
Turning away, she says with a slight trace of annoyance, “Your memories will come back slowly. But know this; they are gone for a good reason. You’ll see in time.”
Cari, who’s been silent all this time approaches her and clutches her arm urgently. Séis looks back to me in sadness.
“Forgive me,” is all she says. She disappears with Cari down a corridor to our left.

~~~~

After my thoughts clear, I turn to my companions.
“Why didn’t you shoot?” I ask them.
Star fiddles with his weapon, “I’m not sure...It didn’t seem right. I’ve had this feeling like I shouldn’t shoot every time I raise my weapon up at that shadow… Séis, or whatever her name is…”
Boop is silently studying the drawings on the walls.
He finally mutters without looking over his shoulder, “What did she do to you, Nick?”
“Another memory… I saw it so clearly. I’m not sure what it means,” I answer slowly.
“It has to mean something. She did say she took your memories from you. That means you’ve been here before. But that seems impossible. This place just formed nearly a week and a few days ago…”
“Unless it was on another planet,” Star exclaims.
I pick up my Mosquito and nod. “It was. Another planet not far from here. In the same galaxy…”
“You’re serious then?! Other planets suitable for life do exist in this galaxy?” Boop says.
My head seems to nod itself in regards to Boop’s question.
We start down the way that Séis left us.
“Why can’t we just make a home out of one of those…we’ve got a decent military force,” Star echoes in an annoyed tone.
I sigh, “I’m pretty sure King Kubrick wouldn’t allow it…”
Her voice echoes in my head.
Think. Why did you come here?

posts.t: [18+] "The Demon from the Underworld", a Story of the Kagome0625.

posts.h:
Chapter 1: The Preparation
It was that month before the end of the Korea World of Brick Galaxy, I knew that we can't last longer in this world but that doesn't mean we give up that easily. One day, we have some news that most soldiers and builders tend to migrate to Europe World. Despite that we may encounter some problem or the people of that World that speaks different languages than us, we had no choice but to migrate to there. But we're not just ready for that yet. I am K-0625 and I am the head leader of the global Blue Fang Team. Highly-trained professional of Mobile Soldier and a Universal Weapon Expert and this may seem to be the time where I have to say good bye to all of my good times from this World. As I head to my room and my office I gathered enough stuff I want to bring as we all migrate to the new World. I decided to look at the large picture hanging on the wall of me posing and saluting at the same time with my Lightning 2. "No Cover, All Man" I said, I continued to pack up my stuff and my gear for the migrations. Then, there was a multiple knocking on the door which signals me that there will be a meeting for all of us. I knew that it was my sister doing that and I know it's time for us to discuss and maybe say the last good bye to this world.

I stopped packing my stuff and head down to the Meeting Hall. There, my sister was waiting for me to sit next to her along with her Mobile Task Force leader, BunnyHawk. As we all sat down with almost all of the Purple Oni Clan members, my sister stood up and spoke. "We have two choices, either we stay nice with them or go full aggressive to the peoples we may encounter." The clan members of the Purple Oni look each other and may choose and decide which of those two choices is a good idea. But then I spoke to my sister "You know it's best to just stay nice, y'know. You know that we're being nice to the United States, so it's best to be nice to the Europe as well... but why either be nice or go aggressive?" my sister replied "Sorry, I somehow have this feeling that comparing them to United States’ I don't think that they are really are the same, despite the different language they both have." BunnyHawk didn't say anything and look on her phone for any news from the Europe World. "It doesn't matter" I said, "But we shall stay nice as always. But in case things have gotten wrong, we go your way, sis." Then the clan members of the Purple Oni nods and decided to rely on my plan and how we shall greet them.

BunnyHawk puts her phone down and messaged me with her sign language as she looked at me: "But you don't seem to be able to compete with them, they are more highly-trained and more skillful than you are." I shook my head and messaged her "The 'Legendaries' shall not boast about our skills and knowledge for this World and theirs" then BunnyHawk nods. My sister spoke "I expected that ALL OF YOU have packed your stuff to be ready to migrate to a new World, we may not see each other however due to the fact the traveling from that world via Portal will have a chance to make some us not make it and end up in fading dusts." The rest of the Purple Oni clan members shudder that hopefully that we all make it successfully without casualties. "I shall check on the Europe World by myself as a scout and comeback for any further news and a good place to set up the portals. The first placed portals ended up in risky way but I'll be re-arranging that alone." Then BunnyHawk looks at me and messaged me: "It will be dangerous to go alone, we may not sure what's out there this time." I then messaged her back "I don't die easily, but expect me that I may comeback with a scratch of my armor." BunnyHawk nods and my sister said "You shall do it once yo-" then I quickly said "I already finished my packing, I will only bring foods, water, and my main weapon of choice." I slowly walk out of the Meeting Hall as my sister continue on the meeting and discussion with the Purple Oni clan.

I went out towards the room where we set out our Portal. I activated the portal and arms myself with Lightning 2 and slowly walks into the Portal. Gladly that the Portal may have recognize me so I don't have to worry about getting myself becoming a pile of fading dust as I proceed to the portal. As time passes by I have finally reached to the United States and the Europe World, I was hoping that I don’t need to worry about some trouble approaching just because I’m displayed as an unrecognized person… boopboop is the only person who remembers me. Gotta make sure I have no else beside him to come by and bring some trouble near the portal…

Chapter 2: The Girl and the Demon.

As I then continue on find a good place to set up our portal coordination as I travel around the woods. I always tend to feel like I’m being watched, but my sonar visions detected none of the Human Brickmans in the distances or nearby, or is it maybe I’m being watched by some other species that lives in the woods…? Well it doesn’t matter.. I just want to know what I just heard when I was sleeping… Even the part or the time when I was sleeping, I was… communicating someone not from mouth to ear… but something like in the dream, or maybe from heart to heart… Although I had this feeling that during the time the world is about to fall apart, I sense that there will be a conflict or a war to make our world to collapse quicker… But I don’t know with who or why a war, but then I was continue on communicating with this person when I was sleeping in my tombstone, but then all in the sudden I woke up.. trying to remember the voice from the person I was communicating with. But none of that matters now, because I have found a perfect coordination for our portal to set for migrations: A field plain, field with maybe some tall grass and flowers, roses, and some tress as well.

But then as I was about to set a coordination for the portal, I hear a sound of a fast arrow flying towards me in a quick speed at my left. As I turned to my left quick, an extremely thin arrow with a large arrowhead passes by my left visor hud, that It was so close it almost touched the front of my mask. I quickly lay down on the tall grass to take cover and load my Lightning 2 and look around with my sonar visions. My sonar visions detects no one around or from far distances, maybe this forest is being watched by some other species that is not human! So I turned off my sonar visions and rely on my own eyes. As I wear off my mask and look around, I feel like someone is standing on me, but not quite heavy. As soon as I realize of what is standing on me, I feel the slight tap on back of my head by what it feels like a Reindeer Crossbow. I knew I’m doomed, but then the person who is standing on my back and pointing the crossbow at the back of my head spoke to me “Who are you, and why are you here?” The voice is officially a female, and quite young. I then answered, “I am the brother of Kagome.. 0615, K-0625.. I am here to uhh, set a good spot for our portal for our migrations to this world.” Then the girl replies, “Kagome 0615..? I heard of her before, so you’re her brother? I didn’t knew that she had a brother before… “. I then answered again, trying not to be stupid, “Yes, this is my second time being in this world… and I am not a threat, so please can you get off of my back and can we see our faces..?” She then nods and jumps off my back and sits down, I then take a small breath and sit up straight then look at her. She has a quite long hair, She seems to be wearing the helmet I have never seen before, her uniform is a Surgeon as well as her pants, and she is armed with a Reindeer Crossbow, but not an ordinary Reindeer Crossbow.

Her Reindeer Crossbow has some line and some art that shines with pure green chroma. The scope is slightly much customized, maybe used for adjusting the distances of the scope perhaps. We both looked each other, then she has talked to me “My name is Melody, you?” Then I answered, “My sister called me Song or MK, but you can call me MK if you want to.” She then stood up and said, “You should go back and do what you have to do, because we are also aware of how your world is about to collapse and of course we did agree that we can welcome your peoples from the migrations to our world.” I then replied, “Thank you, uhh.. Melody. I will. And it was nice to meet you.” “It was nice knowing and seeing you as well, MK.” So then I stood up straight as well and set the coordination of my portal and activate the portal again. “The portal is success, now we can se-” but as I was trying to finish my sentence to Melody, I have a message from my sister, I then looked at the message from my phone and see what’s up.

BirdofPrey: Brother!! WHERE ARE YOU??

BlueDevil: I’m done setting up the coordinate for our perfect spot after the migrations, what’s up?

With those number of soldiers patrolling around the city, I wouldn’t be able to fight them all on in all direction, but with this Micro Rockets: I can.

I quickly got out of the cover as I vault over a car that I was taking cover with and shoot towards the sky multiple time, to alert the Chinese Forces. As they all hear a sudden gunshot, they all scattered and arm themselves with their Tarantula 41s and stay on their guard.

Kagome0625: OH YEAH! THIS. IS. GOING TO BE. FUN!!

I decided to take care of the North road as I fire my Bronto 1000 with an extreme rate of fire and devastating power as I hop and jump above the cars like a rabbit. The weapon is a bit inaccurate than my Lightning 2, but this is really good for taking out a large group of enemy forces. With every bullets I fired they all go land and go for their forehead, their eyes, as well as their mouth. Multiple of enemy forces aim their Tarantula 41s towards me and fires without holding back and hesitation. But, no matter how many time they all fire their weapon towards me, they never manage to lay a single hit to any of part of my body. I then decided to leap towards a nearby tall building’s wall and grips on the wall as I continue to fire my Bronto 1000 towards the North Patrolling squads and continue to count many heads that was blown to pieces with every single rounds of Bronto 1000 I fired to them.

Chapter 9. Part 2

Then the East Patrolling forces arrived at the middle to find out what’s going on, but as soon as they sees me I activated the Micro Rockets Launcher and fires 8 volley of extremely, fast-travelling rockets (and my God they are so small, cute, and deadly) towards the East Patrolling Forces and blow them all to pieces. Half of them survived however, but I quickly jump out of the walls I was gripping on and land in front of the staggered and exploded as I run towards their body and fire my Bronto 1000 so I can make sure that they are really killed in action. One of the fallen and staggered soldiers stood up right by me and tries to slash at me with his bayonet. But as he was about to lay his hand onto my shoulder, I quickly finish him off. I continue to fire more racks of Micro Rockets and my Bronto 1000.

I finished up all of the East Patrolling forces as I then try to wipe out the entire North Patrolling forces, but the West Patrolling forces arrived as I was about to ready to fire my weapon. But then I noticed there is a small button on the base of the Micro Rocket Launchers. It has a label “Bottomless Rockets.” This is telling me that I can fire Micro Rockets indefinitely without requiring a reload, which is like… wow, Have the Drake family evolved much more efficient than the Shark family? But nevermind, I quickly pressed the button as the attachments opens wider as the rack of Micro Rockets then stacks up and turns vibrantly. I reload my Bronto 1000 and begin the Micro Rockets Galore, with 30 Micro Rockets being fired every seconds, 30 powerful explosion around the cities of Gangnam every seconds, and exploding Chinese forces. I sprint, hopped, and continue to fire my Bronto 1000 and the Micro Rocket Launchers at the same time towards the enemy. I laughed maliciously as I see all of these soldiers die. Debris covers the floor. So this is what it feels like for being even much more powerful with just one attachment of the weapon that literally turns all 1,500 Chinese Forces into 15,000 Chinese rice with meat.
